data.name: Preface
entries: No foray into a Star Wars setting is complete without ships. The previous version of this book included the bare minimum, with a series of disjointed rules that I wrote three years ago and layer a thin veneer of polish over. Since it's frst release last summer, this book has undergone a signifcant overhaul to make it more appealing and engaging with players and GMs.
While I've ultimately spent more time on the core content of the Player Handbook and the Expanded Content, this book has been signifcantly more difcult.
Within the context of 5e, what I, and my group, have written here has been uncharted territory. I hope it makes sense.

This book is designed to parallel the 5e Player's Handbook as much as it can. It includes all the relevant chapters, as they relate to the space component of the game. The signifcant diferences will be listed below.
While this expansion utilizes the base rules of 5th Edition, there are signifcant diferences that will be illustrated here, broken down by chapter.

{@book CHAPTER 1: STEP-BY-STEP STARSHIPS|sw5e-sotg|3|Chapter 1: Step-By-Step Starships} This chapter is designed to help you integrate this into your campaign, from the perspective of a player. It helps you to build Han Solo as a Pilot, with his ship the Millennium Falcon.

{@book CHAPTER 2: DEPLOYMENTS|sw5e-sotg|4|Chapter 2: Deployments} Deployments are the certain locations that might exist on a ship, and what actions are granted by manning a deployment. There are fve potential deployments: {@book coordinator|sw5e-sotg|4|Coordinator}, {@book gunner|sw5e-sotg|4|Gunner}, {@book mechanic|sw5e-sotg|4|Mechanic}, {@book operator|sw5e-sotg|4|Operator} and {@book pilot|sw5e-sotg|4|Pilot}. Any character can engage in any deployment, though some characters are more suited to certain deployments.

Additionally, once a player has chosen a favored deployment, they will be able to specialize in that deployment. Specializing in a deployment unlocks features specifc to that deployment via a series of ranks (levels).
{@book CHAPTER 3: STARSHIPS|sw5e-sotg|5|Chapter 3: Starships} This chapter covers the acquisition of a starship, as well as upgrading starships to higher tiers (levels).
Unlike classes, starship tiers are locked to the size category of the starship. Within each starship tier, however, there are choices that let you specialize your ship in a direction of your choice.

{@book CHAPTER 4: MODIFICATIONS|sw5e-sotg|6|Chapter 4: Modifications} As your starship progresses in tiers, it unlocks upgrade slots, which can be spent on upgrades. Upgrades fall into one of fve categories: engineering, operation, suite, universal, and weapon.

{@book CHAPTER 5: EQUIPMENT|sw5e-sotg|7|Chapter 5: Equipment} Equipment functions in a similar capacity to the ground component, with the except of it needing to be integrated into a ship as opposed to just held. There are fve major equipment types: armor, shields, weapons, hyperdrives, and navcomputers.

{@book CHAPTER 6: CUSTOMIZATION OPTIONS|sw5e-sotg|8|Chapter 6: Customization Options} Characters can choose to focus on a single deployment, or multiple deployments via multispeccing. Additionally, as characters unlock ranks in deployments they gain access to ventures (feats).

{@book CHAPTER 7: USING ABILITY SCORES|sw5e-sotg|9|Chapter 7: Using Ability Scores} While deployed in a starship, rather than using their own physical ability scores (Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution), skills will instead use the respective ability score of the ship. As ship's have no mental ability scores (Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma), the players will still use their own.

{@book CHAPTER 8: ADVENTURING|sw5e-sotg|10|Chapter 8: Adventuring} This chapter discusses the adventuring component of space. One new feature, turning speed, has been added. The oversimplifcation is that, unlike players, ships can't easily change directions. In addition to fying speed, ships have a turning speed; in order to turn 90 degrees, the ship must spend that many feet of movement.

{@book CHAPTER 9: COMBAT|sw5e-sotg|11|Chapter 9: Combat} Combat is designed to function similar to combat on the ground; players still roll their own initiative and act on their own turn. The key diference is the actions available to players are keyed to their specifc deployment. For instance, the pilot controls the movement of the ship, and the gunner controls the weapons.
{@book CHAPTER 10: GENERATING ENCOUNTERS|sw5e-sotg|12|Chapter 10: Generating Encounters} This chapter is designed to help GMs build interesting encounters.
{@book APPENDIX A: CONDITIONS|sw5e-sotg|13|Appendix A: Conditions} Conditions adapted to this expansion.
GOING FORWARD This book is signifcantly more play-testy, and thus requires the most review. I hope you'll join the discord and the discussion, and help the community move this content forward.

data.name: Introduction
entries: The {@i Star Wars} 5th Edition roleplaying game is about storytelling in worlds of lightsabers and the Force. It shares elements with childhood games of make-believe. Like those games, SW5e is driven by imagination. It's about picturing the towering AT-AT beneath the stormy night sky and imagining how a squad of rebel troops might overcome the challenges that scene presents.

This book is designed to add another significant layer to your SW5e experience. The rules are designed to work alongside the traditional SW5e ruleset, and so an experienced player should have no trouble jumping right into the book. For the less experienced-or more curious-player, this Introduction discusses the basics.

{@b Game Master (GM):} As your ship exits hyperspace above the moon of Nar Shaddaa, you see a series of snubfighters move to approach your freighter in an offensive formation. Several other craft go about their business in the vicinity, paying no attention to your potential predicament.
{@b Rickey (playing Vinto):} I want to hail them and see what their intentions are.
{@b Drew (playing Dash):} I'm going to go man the dorsal gun, just in case.
{@b Erik (playing Kodo):} ...

Unlike a game of make-believe, D&D gives structure to the stories, a way of determining the consequences of the adventurers' actions. Players roll dice to resolve whether their attacks hit or miss or whether their starship can scale a skim the surface of a star destroyer, break the lock on a concussion missile, or pull off some other dangerous task. Anything is possible, but the dice make some outcomes more probable than others.
{@b Game Master (GM):} OK, one at a time. Rickey, you're hailing the newcomers?
{@b Rickey:} Yeah. Do they respond?
{@b GM:} Make a Charisma check.
{@b Rickey:} Does my {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb} skill apply?
{@b GM:} Sure!
{@b Rickey (rolling a d20):} ... Four.
{@b GM:} You can hear the click of static, but no voice responds to you. And Drew, Dash is manning the dorsal gun?
{@b Drew:} Yup!
{@b GM:} Okay. Eric, what's Kodo doing?
{@b Eric:} ...

In the {@i Star Wars} Dungeons and Dragons game, each player creates an adventurer (also called a character) and teams up with other adventurers (played by friends). Working together, the group might obtain a freighter and take to the stars, expanding the scope and potential of their game. They might become pirates, the scourge of the Outer Rim, or they may accept missions from a leading faction. They may become smugglers, taking jobs as they see fit, or become bounty hunters in the employee of a powerful hutt.

One player, however, takes on the role of the Game Master (GM), the game's lead storyteller and referee. The GM creates adventures for the characters, who navigate its hazards and decide which paths to explore. The GM might describe an ongoing naval battle, and the players decide what they want their adventurers to do. Will they choose a side and join in the combat? Will they attempt to mediate a truce? Or will they simply choose a new destination?

Then the GM determines the results of the adventurers' actions and narrates what they experience. Because the GM can improvise to react to anything the players attempt, D&D is infinitely flexible, and each adventure can be exciting and unexpected.

The game has no real end; when one story or quest wraps up, another one can begin, creating an ongoing story called a {@b campaign}. Many people who play the game keep their campaigns going for months or years, meeting with their friends every week or so to pick up the story where they left off. The adventurers grow in might as the campaign continues. Each force defeated, each adventure completed, and each relic recovered not only adds to the continuing story, but also earns the adventurers new capabilities. This increase in power is reflected by an adventurer's level and deployment rank, as well as their starship's tier.

There's no winning and losing in the {@i Star Wars} Dungeons and Dragons game—at least, not the way those terms are usually understood. Together, the GM and the players create an exciting story of bold adventurers who confront deadly perils. Sometimes an adventurer might come to a grisly end, dispatched by a Sith lord. The party itself might meet its demise should it bite off more than it can chew in a starship encounter. Even so, the other adventurers can beseech a powerful Jedi to revive their fallen comrade, or the players might choose (or be forced) to create new characters to carry on. The group might fail to complete an adventure successfully, but if everyone had a good time and created a memorable story, they all win.

entries.name: Take to the Stars
entries: One of the premier components of {@i Star Wars} 5th Edition, versus a traditional Dungeons and Dragons campaign, is the wide variety of planets a character can visit and explore. To facilitate and encourage that experience, adventurers need a means to travel.

Public transportation exists, and players can simply pay someone else to transport them if they so desire. Alternatively, you can elect to keep the scope of a campaign small, and limit it to one or two planets. It would be easy to run a game on Coruscant, with its myriad cultures and territories, without the players having to venture offworld.
But if your players want to journey among the stars, this book is designed to those ends.

entries.name: Using This Book
entries: {@i Starships of the Galaxy} is divided into ten chapters.

{@book Chapters 1-6|sw5e-sotg|3|Chapter 1: Step-By-Step Starships} are about taking your SW5e character, adopting a deployment, and designing a ship. It includes information on the six main deployments, the six ship size classifications, ship upgrades, ship equipment, and the customization options that you can choose from. Many of the rules in these chapters rely on material found later in the book. If you come across a game concept that you don't understand, consult the book's table of contents.
For initial encounters, you can generally skip these chapters by running characters without a deployment and by utilizing a pre-generated stock ship.

{@book Chapters 7-9|sw5e-sotg|9|Chapter 7: Using Ability Scores} detail the rules of how to run the space portion of the game, beyond the basics described in this introduction. These chapters covers where the rules deviate from the ground game, and where they remain the same.

{@book Chapter 10|sw5e-sotg|12|Chapter 10: Generating Encounters} is for GMs, and covers the rules for generating encounters and ships, as well as the stats for stock ships off which players can build.

entries.name: How to Play
entries: Generally, the space game runs almost identical to the ground. The GM still describes the environment, and the players describe what they want to do. The GM then narrates the results of of the adventurers' actions.

entries.name: Space Versus Ground
entries: The most important distinction here is the scaling down of the dice. An X-wing's laser cannon deals 1d6 to an enemy X-wing. The perspective for damage here is space. If you need to scale ships to the perspective of players, see {@variantrule Space Versus Ground Scale|sw5e-sotg}. You typically scale damage, {@variantrule Hull Points|sw5e-sotg|hull points}, {@variantrule Shield Points|sw5e-sotg|shield points}, damage reduction, and shield regeneration rate of ships by 10, and vice versa. For Instance, an X-wing's primary weapon may deal 1d6 to ships, but would deal (1d6)x10 to a player, while a player's explosion power would instead deal (8d6)/10 damage (round down) to the X-wing. Because of their size and durability, some GMs may rule that Large and larger ships are simply immune to damage from small arms fire. Additionally, a Tiny starship is Tiny on the space scale, but Huge on the ground scale. Consequently, a Small ship is Gargantuan on the ground scale. Medium and larger ships would be considered colossal. Because starships are not primarily designed to fight individual creatures, Tiny-Large Starships have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on attacks versus Large and smaller creatures (and such creatures have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on saves caused by these ships' weapons).

entries.name: Game Dice
entries: The game uses the same polyhedral dice with different numbers of sides, referenced in the same fashion; the different dice are referred to by the letter d followed by the number of sides: d2, {@dice d4}, {@dice d6}, {@dice d8}, {@dice d10}, {@dice d12}, and {@dice d20}.

entries.name: The D20
entries: The same {@dice d20} that a Jedi uses to swing his lightsaber is used for firing a ship's weapons. The biggest deviation here is that when a player fires a ship weapon, they use the player's {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, {@i but the ship's Wisdom bonus}. The reason for this is two-fold: {@b 1. In the ground game, some Ability scores are stronger than others.} Since this ruleset is designed to enhance the way the game is played, one character should not be penalized for being slightly different from another character.

{@b 2. How accurate a ship's weapons are is modified by the ship's targeting system.} A ship with a higher Wisdom is more capable of accurate targeting than a ship with a low Wisdom, consequently yielding a greater likelihood of accuracy.
This and other deviations will be discussed at greater length in {@book Chapter 7: Using Ability Scores|sw5e-sotg|9|Chapter 7: Using Ability Scores}.

entries.name: Advantage and Disadvantage
entries: {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb} and {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb} function identical to the ground game; with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}, you roll two dice and take the higher value, while with the {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} you roll two dice and take the lesser.

entries.name: Specific Beats General
entries: In the same vein, while latter chapters contain broad strokes for the game's rules, certain deployment or ship features override those rules, creating an exception to how the rest of the game works. Remember this: if a specific rule contradicts a general rule, the specific rule wins.

entries.name: ROUND APPROPRIATELY
entries: Follow standard rules for rounding; if a number ends in one-half or greater, round up, while if a number ends in less than one-half, round down.

entries.name: What It Brings
entries: {@b Starships of the Galaxy} is designed to be an {@i in addition to} rather than {@i instead of}. The rules here, predominantly, function identically, or analogously, to the ground game, but the features and boons achieved here are designed to be kept separate. While features of the ground game, such as your characters' species, classes, backgrounds, and customization options impact your character's prowess in the space game, the space game should not affect your characters in the ground game.

As always, there might be some exceptions to this rule; for instance, many of the suite options offer bonuses that affect the ground game, and players can use their ship to assault a stronghold that their characters might not be able to conquer on their own. Ultimately, the cross over is up to the GM to adjudicate.

data.name: Chapter 1: Step-By-Step Starships
entries: Your first step in transitioning to the space portion of your {@i Star Wars} 5th Edition campaign is imagining how having a starship impacts your character. When participating in the space portion of the game, your character is impacted by a number of features, including their chosen deployment, the size and style of ship on which they adventure, and the modification and equipment that ship has access to. These choices can enhance and enrich your avatar.

Before you dive into step 1 below, think about where your adventurer would be most likely to participate in a starship. You might be a dauntless {@book ace pilot|sw5e-sotg|4|Pilot}, or a crushing {@book gunner|sw5e-sotg|4|Gunner}. Perhaps you are a genius {@book mechanic|sw5e-sotg|4|Mechanic}, an intricate {@book operator|sw5e-sotg|4|Operator}, or a charming {@book coordinator|sw5e-sotg|4|Coordinator}. Maybe you are interested in a mixture of these roles.

Additionally, what kind of ship, and your intended purpose, can impact these decisions. Do you want to be a soldier in the Imperial Navy, piloting a TIE fighter and leading a squadron? Or are you more inclined to travel as a mercenary aboard a light freighter, taking jobs as you see fit in order to keep your ship in space? Maybe you instead want to be a bounty hunter in an assault craft, tracking your quarry to the Outer Rim, and beyond?

Once you have an idea in mind, follow these steps in order, making decisions that reflect the character and ship you want. Your conception of your character and starship might evolve with each choice you make. What's important is that you come to the table with a character you're excited to play.

Throughout this section, we use the term {@b deployment sheet} and {@b starship sheet} to mean whatever you use to track your character and starship, respectively, whether it's a formal sheet (like the ones at the end of these rules), some form of digital record, or a piece of notebook paper. The official SW5e sheets are a fine place to start until you know what information you need and how you use it during the game.

entries.name: Building the Millennium Falcon
entries: Each step of ship/crew creation includes an example of that step, with a player building the iconic starship the Millennium Falcon, as it is portrayed during the events of Episode IV.

entries.name: Acquire a Starship
entries: A crew is nothing without its starship, and this chapter covers the acquisition and initial set up of starships. Like classes and deployments, starships have their own features that are driven by their size category. {@book Chapter 3: Starships|sw5e-sotg|5|Chapter 3: Starships} provides more information about acquiring a starship, Starship Size Categories, and starship features.

What starship you acquire is the second impactful decision you make when you adopt the space portion of your campaign. Each size category of starship has unique and tangible features, and determines what kind of crew your starship can support. A Small starship, for instance, can support 1-2 crew members at tier 0, while a Medium starship can support an entire adventuring party. At larger sizes, the crew shifts into the hundreds and thousands of crew members a ship can support.

entries.name: Tier
entries: Once you've obtained your starship—through any number of ways—you gain the ability to upgrade your ship. Typically, like deployments, starships are obtained at tier 0. A tier 0 ship is typically newly constructed, or otherwise not yet battle-tested or broken in.

Starting off at tier 0 marks the beginning of your starship's journey and evolution. Over time, with the use of resources and workers—and credits—a starship can be upgraded from tier 0 all the way up to tier 5, unlocking unique features—and choices—as it improves.

entries.name: Hull Points and Hull Dice
entries: Your starship's hull points define how tough your ship's hull is in combat and other dangerous situations. Your hull points are determined by your Hull Dice (short for Hull Point Dice).

At tier 0, your starship has a varying quantity and size of Hull Dice, depending on its size category. Your starship starts with hull points equal to the highest roll of that die, as well as the average roll for each additional Hull Die. You also add your Constitution modifier to each die. This is your {@b hull point maximum}.

Record your starship's hull points on your starship sheet. Also record the type of Hull Die your starship uses and the number of Hull Dice it has. After you conduct refitting—and at certain other points—you can spend Hull Dice to regain hull points (see  “RECHARGING AND REFITTING” in {@book Chapter 8: Adventuring|sw5e-sotg|10|Chapter 8: Adventuring}).

entries.name: Shield Points and Shield Dice
entries: Most starships also have shields, although they do not come standard, and their strength—your ship's {@b shield point maximum}—and the amount they can regenerate each round—your ship's {@b shield regeneration rate}—is determined partially by your shield Dice, your ship's Strength modifier, and your choice of shields, detailed in {@book Chapter 5: Equipment|sw5e-sotg|7|Chapter 5: Equipment}.  The number and type of shield dice normally parallels your Hull Dice.

entries.name: Building the Millennium Falcon, Step 1
entries: The Millennium Falcon is a heavily modified YT-1300f light freighter, and falls under the Medium size category. The ship starts at tier 0. As a tier 0 Medium ship, the Millennium Falcon chooses a role, granting a +1 ASI. We choose "freighter," granting a +1 to the Falcon's Constitution score. As a tier 0 Medium ship, the Millennium Falcon has 5 Hull Dice - which are d8s - and a Constitution modifier of +1. Consequently, the Millennium Falcon has 33 hull points: 8 + the average for the subsequent four dice (5) + the Constitution modifier for each Hull Die (5 x 1). The Millennium Falcon has shields, so we turn to {@book Chapter 5: Equipment|sw5e-sotg|7|Chapter 5: Equipment} and turn to the "{@book Shields|sw5e-sotg|7|Shields}" section. We select fortress shields to represent the Falcon's very powerful shield systems. As a tier 0 Medium ship, the Falcon has 5 shield Dice - which are d8s - and a Strength modifier of +2. Consequently, the Falcon has 38 Base shield Points: 8 + the average for the subsequent four dice (5) + the Strength modifier for each shield Die (5 x 2). Because fortress shields multiply your Base shield Points by 3/2, the Falcon has a shield Capacity of 57. The Falcon's shield Regeneration rate is 5: the shield die maximum (8) multiplied by the fortress shield shield Regeneration Rate Coefficient (2/3). When the Millennium Falcon progresses to tier 1 it gains the following features: Starship Improvements and Evasive Maneuvers. We record Evasive Maneuvers on the starship sheet. Since the Millennium Falcon is fast, we increase its Strength by 2 with the Ability Score Improvement. This increases the Falcon's Strength Modifier by 1 to +3, adding 5 more to the ship's Base shield Points. It gains an additional Hull Dice, and it’s current and maximum hull points increases by 6. It also gains an additional shield Die, increasing its Base shield Points by another 8 (5+3). Recalculating the Falcon's shield Capacity gives us 76. Additionally, at tier 0, a Medium ship gets a choice of two {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} proficiencies. For the Falcon, we choose Strength and Dexterity.

entries.name: Determine Ability Scores
entries: Much of what your ship does in the game depends on its six abilities: Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma. Each ability has a score, which is a number you record on your character sheet.

The six abilities and their use in the game are described in {@book Chapter 7: Using Ability Scores|sw5e-sotg|9|Chapter 7: Using Ability Scores}. The {@b Ability Score Summary} table provides a quick reference for what qualities are measured by each ability.  Ships size categories decrease and/or increase the base ability scores, as can tier advancements and ship modifications.

You generate your shipís six ability scores using a standard array of ability scores that you assign to each ability as you wish (Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma): 15, 14, 13, 12, 10, 8. Afterward, make any changes to your ability scores as a result of your ship size.

After assigning your ability scores, determine your ability modifiers using the {@b Ability Scores and Modifiers} table. To determine an ability modifier without consulting the table, subtract 10 from the ability score and then divide the result by 2 (round down). Write the modifier next to each of your scores.

entries.name: Building The Millennium Falcon, Step 2
entries: We will use the standard set of scores (15, 14, 13, 12, 10, 8) for the Falconís abilities. The Falcon is fast nimble, so weíll put it's highest scores, 15 and 14, in Strength and Dexterity, respectively. We then apply the 13 to Intelligence, the 12 to Constitution, the 10 to Wisdom and the 8 to Charisma. Because Medium ships have no ability score adjustments, The Falcon's Ability Scores and Modifiers look like this: Strength 15 (+2), Dexterity 14 (+2), Constitution 12 (+1), Intelligence 13 (+1), Wisdom 10 (+0), Charisma 8 (-1).

entries.name: Variant: Customizing Ability Scores
entries: At your Game Masterís option, you can use this variant for determining your ship's ability scores. The method described here allows you to build a ship with a set of ability scores you choose individually.

You have 27 points to spend on your ability scores. The cost of each score is shown on the {@b Ability Score Point Cost} table. For example, a score of 14 costs 7 points. Using this method, 15 is the highest ability score you can end up with, before applying special increases. You canít have a score lower than 8.

This method of determining ability scores enables you to create a set of three high numbers and three low ones (15, 15, 15, 8, 8, 8), a set of numbers that are above average and nearly equal (13, 13, 13, 12, 12, 12), or any set of numbers between those extremes.

entries.name: Installing Modifications
entries: Your starship includes a number of standard modifications, and can include more modifications—at the expense of credits, workers, and time—enhancing and augmenting the ship's functionality. Modifications fall into five categories: engineering, operation, suite, universal, and weapon. {@book Chapter 4: Modifications|sw5e-sotg|6|Chapter 4: Modifications} provides more information about these categories and installation costs.

entries.name: Building the Millennium Falcon, Step 3
entries: At tier 0, the Millennium Falcon comes with one suite at no cost, so we add a Barracks. Additionally, we choose a Living Quarters to give the crew their own rooms. We also choose the Recreation and Storage Compartment suites, bringing the total modifications to 3. The Millennium Falcon has dorsal and ventral cannons, so we choose two Fixed Hardpoints. Additionally, these are turrets that can fire in a 360 degree arc, so we add two turret mountings, both with direct control mods. We're up to 9 modifications. She has a Hyperdrive and Navcomputer, bringing the total modifications to 11. Finally, the Falcon has exterior protection, so we take the Anti-Boarding System as our 12th mod. As Han gains credits, he continues to upgrade the ship, eventually installing an Improved Navcomputer modification, two weapon slave arrays to allow firing the turrets from the cockpit, and another fixed hardpoint.

entries.name: Choose Equipment
entries: Starships have access to certain types of equipment. Every starship has access to armor and shields as well as a reactor and a power coupling system, and most have access to weapons. Many starships, especially larger ones, have access to hyperdrives and navcomputers. The {@b Equipment} chapter provides more information on these categories.

entries.name: Armor Class
entries: Your {@b Armor Class} (AC) represents how well your starship avoids being damaged in battle—either my avoiding being hit entirely or by remaining essentially unharmed from an attack. Your AC is determined by four major factors: your base AC, your starship's Dexterity modifier, your ship's Tier bonuses, and the type of armor your ship has installed (see {@book Chapter 5: Equipment|sw5e-sotg|7|Chapter 5: Equipment} and {@book Chapter 4: Modifications|sw5e-sotg|6|Chapter 4: Modifications}).

Your ship has a base AC of 10. You then add (or subtract) the other factors above: Dexterity modifier, potentially limited by the type of armor you have installed; your ship's Tier bonus, if any; and any applicable modifications.

entries.name: Weapons
entries: Your ship can have a number of weapons no greater than the number of fixed hardpoints it has. For each fixed hardpoint, a single weapon can be attached. When making {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}, or setting the save DC for ship weapons, we use the starship's Wisdom modifier, and the crew's {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. We also add the ship's Strength modifier to damage rolls.

entries.name: Building the Millennium Falcon, Step 4
entries: The Millennium Falcon has a base AC of 10. The Falcon comes with deflection armor installed, which allows the ship to add up to a +2 Dexterity bonus.  With a Dexterity of 14, we add 2 to the Millennium Falcon's base {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb|armor class} for a total of 12 at Tier 1. The Falcon has two turreted hardpoints, and we choose traditional quad laser cannons to equip to them. When making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with either weapon, we use the ship's Wisdom modifier (+1) and the crew's {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} (+3, e.g.). When making a damage roll, we add the ship's Strength modifier (+3). The fixed hardpoint is equipped with a missile launcher and is loaded with concussion missiles.  The missile's {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} has a DC equal to 8 plus the ship's Wisdom modifier (+1) and the crew's {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} (+3). We note that the quad laser cannons have an unlimited firing arc, do 2d4 + 3 energy damage, have a range of 800/3200, can fire in rapid mode, and overheat after shooting 8 shots.  The concussion missiles have a limited firing arc, do 2d8 + 3 energy damage, have a range of 600/2400 and must fire in either burst 1 or rapid mode.  These Falcon can fire 8 missiles before needing to be reloaded, and these missiles have the "explosive" feature, which will force {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} checks by characters on affected ships.

entries.name: Come Together
entries: Most Star Wars characters don't work alone, and while some starships can be operated by a single crew member, it is more dynamic—and engaging—to crew a starship with a {@i party}—each member of the party fulfilling a needed role on the ship. Teamwork and cooperation greatly improve your party's chance to survive the unapologetic lethality of spacefaring.

entries.name: Deployments
entries: There are six major roles directly tied to the control of a starship: coordinator, gunner, mechanic, operator, pilot, and technician.  Any character can have ranks in any one or more deployments and any character can fulfill any one or more roles on a ship at any given time, but because there are only some functions a pilot can access, one character must be at the helm, whether or not the character has any ranks in Pilot. How your character interacts with your ship—or enemy ships—is determined by what they decide to do on any particular turn, but characters will usually begin to focus on one or two particular roles. {@book Chapter 2: Deployments|sw5e-sotg|4|Chapter 2: Deployments} provides more information about each deployment.

The deployment you choose may be the first impactful decision you make when you adopt the space portion of your campaign. Each of the six deployments has a unique and tangible function, and many of them interact—and synergize—with your character's species and class features. As you progress through the ranks of your chosen deployment, you unlock unique features that augment and enhance your interaction with that deployment, potentially granting you new actions, or simply improving the actions already available to your deployment.

entries.name: Rank
entries: Typically, a character starts their space journey at deployment rank 0, and advances through the ranks (up to 5th) over time. A rank 0 character is typically inexperienced in the ways of their starship, although he or she might have been on a starship previously.

Starting off at rank 0 marks your character's entry in the spacefarer life. If you're already familiar with the game, or if you are joining an existing SW5e campaign, your DM might decide to have you begin at a higher rank, on assumption that your character has already survived a few harrowing adventures. Record your rank on your deployment sheet. If you're starting at a higher rank, record the additional elements your deployment specialization grants you.

entries.name: Building the Millennium Falcon, Step 5
entries: A ship is no good without a crew, especially her pilot: Han Solo in this case. Han is a versatile character aboard a ship, but he is strongest in the piloting role (best in the galaxy). When Han achieves his first rank, we spend that rank in the pilot deployment specialization, unlocking the {@book Piloting Procedure|sw5e-sotg|4|Piloting Procedure} and Venture deployment features. For his {@book Piloting Procedure|sw5e-sotg|4|Piloting Procedure}, we mark that Han's power dice are d4s. Additionally, Han knows two tactics: for these we choose Koiogran Turn and {@book Snap Roll|sw5e-sotg|4|Snap Roll}. For his {@book Venture|sw5e-sotg|8|Ventures}, we choose {@optfeature Precision GUNNER|sw5e-sotg}.

entries.name: Beyond the Basics
entries: As your characters—and their starship—go on adventures and overcome challenges, they can increase in their ranks and tiers, respectively. While tiers are driven by the amount of effort—and credits—directly applied to the starship, ranks are earned separately.

Typically, characters start at deployment rank 0, achieving rank 1 after completing their first successful encounter and earning prestige. The GM may decide, however, that characters start at 1st rank or higher, depending on choices in a character's background or during an adventure. Higher ranks are achieved by successfully completing more encounters and earning more prestige, as shown below in the {@b Deployment Rank Prestige} table.

entries.name: Deployment Rank Prestige
entries: Anything that requires the characters to exercise their skills yields prestige. Defeating, routing, or escaping an encounter are the most common methods, but other actions might yield prestige at the discretion of the GM; completing a training simulation or successfully talking your way out of a situation might earn you prestige, for instance.

entries.name: Beyond 5th Rank
entries: Characters who reach 5th rank across their deployments may want to continue progressing in their starship skills. Additional prestige earned can yield additional ranks, though no character can gain higher than 5th rank in any deployment. For each rank beyond 5th, the amount of required prestige increases by 4; achieving 6th rank would require an additional 8 prestige (24 total), while achieving 7th rank would require an additional 12 prestige (36 total).

The expectation is to tie ranks—and hopefully tiers—to proficiency bonuses. When characters reach 5th-level, their {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} increases to 3, and again at 9th (4), 13th (5), and 17th (6). Ranks 2-4 are designed to be awarded at or around those same improvements.

entries.name: Features and Hull/Shield Dice
entries: When your starship gains a tier, it unlocks additional features, depending on its size, as detailed in the description. Some of these features allow you to increase your starship's ability scores. You can't increase an ability score above 20 unless otherwise noted.

Each time your starship gains a tier, it gains gain 1 additional Hull Die and 1 additional shield Die. Roll the Hull Die, add your ship's Constitution modifier to the roll, and add the total to your hull point maximum. Next, roll the shield Die, add your ship's Stength modifier to the roll, and add the total to your base shield points which is then multiplied by the appropriate factor depending on which shields your ship has.  Alternatively, for both hull and shields, you can use the fixed value shown in your class entry, which is the average result of the die roll (rounded up).

When your ship's Constitution modifier increases by 1, its hull point maximum increases by 1 for each Hull Die it has. For example, if your tier 0 Medium ship has a Constitution score of 14, when it reaches tier 1, you increases its Constitution score from 14 to 16, thus increasing its Constitution modifier from +2 to +3. At tier 0, your Medium starship has a total of 6 Hull Dice, so its hull point maximum then increases by 6. The same rules apply to your base shield points and your Strength score.

data.name: Chapter 2: Deployments
entries: Adventurers are extraordinary people, driven by a thirst for excitement into a life that others would never dare lead. They are heroes, compelled to explore the dark places of the world and take on the challenges that lesser women and men can't stand against.

Deployments are roles your characters can fill that are not directly correlated with their class. A character can then specialize in a specific deployment, granting a variety of features, such as the gunner's gambits or the pilot's tactics. As you progress in your deployment specialization, you gain more powerful features, and some features improve. Each deployment specialization entry in this chapter includes a table summarizing the benefits you gain at every rank, and a detailed explanation of each one.
A character can fill multiple roles simultaneously, provided it can reach the appropriate equipment to utilize that deployment's features.

Unlike classes, when players achieve the space portion of the game, they start at rank 0. Players should attempt to experience multiple roles to see which suits them best before choosing the one in which they will specialize.
When engaging in the space portion of a campaign, many class features work in conjunction with a ship deployment, while others don't. It is up to your GM to determine which is which.

entries.name: Venture
entries: Beginning when you choose this deployment as your specialty, at 1st rank, and again at 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th rank, you can choose a venture (see {@book chapter 6|sw5e-sotg|8|Chapter 6: Customization Options} for a list of ventures).

entries.name: {@book Coordinating Leadership|sw5e-sotg|4|Coordinating Leadership}
entries: Also at 1st rank, you learn collaborations that are fueled by special dice called power dice.

entries.name: Collaborations
entries: You learn two collaborations of your choice, which are detailed under "Collaborations" below. You can use only one collaboration per turn, and you can only use each collaboration once per round.
You learn an additional collaboration at 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th rank in this deployment. Each time you learn a new collaboration, you can also replace one collaboration you know with a different one.

entries.name: Power Dice
entries: A power die is expended when you use it. Your ship must have a power die at the required system in order to use the collaboration.

Your ship gains power dice based primarily on reactor production.  These power dice are stored in a central and/or system capacitors to power abilities of crewmembers.  Your power die type is determined by your ship tier.

entries.name: Collaborations
entries: The collaborations are presented in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Battle Stations
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Comms} If you are surprised at the start of combat and aren't {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated}, you can expend one power die to act normally. Additionally, on your first turn in combat, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} you can choose a number of creatures equal to the amount rolled on the power die who can see or hear you to act normally on their first turn.

entries.name: Bolster
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Comms} On your turn, you can use your action and expend one power die to bolster the resolve of the crew of your or another allied ship. That ship gains temporary {@variantrule Hull Points|sw5e-sotg|hull points} equal to the power die roll + your Charisma modifier.

entries.name: Call for Backup
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Comms} When a ship makes an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against your ship, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and expend a power die and command another willing ally ship within 300 feet of the enemy ship to intercede. A crewmember on that allied ship manning a weapon station must use their {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to do so. The enemy ship is then forced to make an attack on the ally ship instead. If the attack misses, the crewmember can immediately make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} against the enemy ship as a part of that same {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}. Roll the power die, and add the result to the ally's {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}.

entries.name: Head's Up
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Comms} When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} and you are not surprised, you can expend a power die and add the number rolled to the {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} of any friendly ship including your own.

entries.name: Incite
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Comms} On your turn, you can use an action and expend one Power die to bolster the resolve of a crew on your or another allied ship who can see or hear you. The allied ship can add your ship's Charisma modifier to a number of damage rolls they make until the start of your next turn equal to the number rolled on the die.

entries.name: Overwhelming Presence
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Comms} As an action, you can make a Charisma ({@skill Impress|sw5e-sotg}) or Charisma ({@skill Menace|sw5e-sotg}) skill check and expend one power die to attempt to charm or frighten a humanoid creature who can see and perceive your ship within 600 feet. Add the power die to the roll. The target makes a contested Intelligence ({@skill Probe|sw5e-sotg}) check. If your check succeeds, the target is {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} by you if you used Impress, or {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} of you if you used Menace, until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Steady As She Goes
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Comms} As an action, you can expend one power die to strengthen your allies' defenses. Roll a power die. Until the end of your next turn, your ship and all allied ships within 500 feet of you when you use this action have a bonus to any {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} they make equal to the amount rolled.

entries.name: Watch Out
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Comms} When a friendly ship, including your own, who can see or hear you makes a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and expend a power die, adding the number rolled to the result of the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. You can use this collaboration before or after making the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, but before any effects of the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} are determined.

entries.name: {@book Uplifting Directive|sw5e-sotg|4|Uplifting Directive}
entries: At 2nd rank, when you take the {@variantrule Direct|sw5e-sotg} action, roll a {@dice d20}. Note the number on the {@dice d20}. This becomes your uplifting directive number.

While you have an uplifting directive number, when an ally makes an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} or {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} affected by your Direct action, you can replace the result of a {@dice d20} roll with the value of the uplifting directive roll. You can use this feature before or after making the roll, but before any effects of the roll are determined. You can only have one uplifting directive roll at a time, and you lose any unused uplifting directive rolls when you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: {@book Inspiring Display|sw5e-sotg|4|Inspiring Display}
entries: Also at 2nd rank, you can inspire others through stirring words. You spend the next minute rallying your allies by giving an inspiring speech. You grant a number of ships up to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} temporary hull points equal to your Charisma modifier.  You also grant to a number of crewmembers up to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} from those ships one {@book Inspiring Display|sw5e-sotg|4|Inspiring Display} die, a {@dice d6}. Once within the next 10 minutes, the creature can roll the die and add the number rolled to one {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} it makes. The creature can wait until after it rolls the {@dice d20} before deciding to use the {@book Inspiring Display|sw5e-sotg|4|Inspiring Display} die, but must decide before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. Once the {@book Inspiring Display|sw5e-sotg|4|Inspiring Display} die is rolled, it is lost. A creature can have only one {@book Inspiring Display|sw5e-sotg|4|Inspiring Display} die at a time.
Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

Your {@book Inspiring Display|sw5e-sotg|4|Inspiring Display} die changes when you reach certain ranks in this deployment. The die becomes a {@dice d8} at 3rd rank, a {@dice d10} at 4th rank, and a {@dice d12} at 5th rank.

entries.name: {@book Rallying Cry|sw5e-sotg|4|Rallying Cry}
entries: At 3rd rank, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can extend a rallying cry to those that can hear you. Choose a number of friendly creatures up to twice your Charisma modifier that can see or hear you. Each of those creatures gains an {@book Inspiring Display|sw5e-sotg|4|Inspiring Display} die that lasts until the end of your next turn.
Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: {@book Masterful Directive|sw5e-sotg|4|Masterful Directive}
entries: Also at 3rd rank, when you roll your uplifting directive number as a part of the Direct action, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to increase your uplifting directive number by an amount equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. If this would increase the value of your uplifting directive number to more than 20, it instead becomes 20.

entries.name: {@book Commanding Presence|sw5e-sotg|4|Commanding Presence}
entries: At 4th rank, you learn a new way to use your {@book Inspiring Display|sw5e-sotg|4|Inspiring Display}. While aboard your ship, when a creature that can see or hear you fails an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can use use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to aid that creature provided it did not already have or use an {@book Inspiring Display|sw5e-sotg|4|Inspiring Display} die this turn. The creature can then roll the die and add it to the result.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain any expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: {@book Contingency Plan|sw5e-sotg|4|Contingency Plan}
entries: Also at 4th rank, while aboard your ship, you can choose two allies, instead of one, when you take the {@variantrule Direct|sw5e-sotg} action.

entries.name: {@book Paragon Coordinator|sw5e-sotg|4|Paragon Coordinator}
entries: As of 5th tier, you are a paragon of your deployment. When you would expend a Power die or an {@book Inspiring Display|sw5e-sotg|4|Inspiring Display} die, you can use a {@dice d4} instead of expending a die. You can only use this feature once per round.

entries.name: {@book Leader Extraordinaire|sw5e-sotg|4|Leader Extraordinaire}
entries: You regain all expended uses of your {@book Inspiring Display|sw5e-sotg|4|Inspiring Display}, {@book Rallying Cry|sw5e-sotg|4|Rallying Cry}, and {@book Commanding Presence|sw5e-sotg|4|Commanding Presence} features when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

Additionally, when you roll an {@book Uplifting Directive|sw5e-sotg|4|Uplifting Directive} number, you can take the maximum instead of rolling. You can use this feature before or after making the roll, but before any effects of the roll are determined. Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

Finally, when a creature uses an {@book Inspiring Display|sw5e-sotg|4|Inspiring Display} die, they take the maximum instead of rolling.  Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Venture
entries: Beginning when you choose this deployment as your specialty, at 1st rank, and again at 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th rank, you can choose a venture (see {@book chapter 6|sw5e-sotg|8|Chapter 6: Customization Options} for a list of ventures).

entries.name: {@book Gunner Techniques|sw5e-sotg|4|Gunner Techniques}
entries: Also at 1st rank, you learn gambits that are fueled by special dice called power dice.

entries.name: Gambits
entries: You learn two gambits of your choice, which are detailed under "Gambits" below. Many gambits enhance an attack in some way. You can use only one gambit per attack, and you can only use each gambit once per turn.
You learn an additional gambit at 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th rank in this deployment. Each time you learn a new gambit, you can also replace one gambit you know with a different one.

entries.name: Power Dice
entries: A power die is expended when you use it. Your ship must have a power die at the required system in order to use the gambit.

Your ship gains power dice based primarily on reactor production.  These power dice are stored in a central and/or system capacitors to power abilities of crewmembers.  Your power die type is determined by your ship tier.

entries.name: Gambits
entries: The gambits are presented in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Crippling Shot
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Weapons} When you hit a ship with a ship attack, you can expend one power die to cripple it. Add the power die to the attack's damage roll, and the target ship's flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is reduced by half until the end of their next turn.

entries.name: Disabling Shot
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Weapons} When you make a ship {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against a ship, you can expend one power die to add it to the roll. On a hit, the ship has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the next {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} or {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} it makes before the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Distracting Shot
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Weapons} When you hit a ship with a ship attack, you can expend one power die to give your allies an opening. You add the power die to the attack's damage roll, and the next {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against the target by someone other than you has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} if the attack is made before the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Explosive Shot
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Weapons} When you reduce a ship to 0 {@variantrule Hull Points|sw5e-sotg|hull points}, you can expend one power die and use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on your turn to make one additional ship attack against a different ship within range. If that attack hits, add the power die to the attack's damage roll.

entries.name: Expose Weakness
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Weapons} When you hit a ship with a ship attack, you can expend a power die and deal additional damage equal to the number rolled. This damage cannot be reduced in any way.

entries.name: Feinting Shot
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Weapons} You can expend one power die and use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on your turn to feint, choosing one ship within your primary weapon's normal range as your target. You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your next {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against that ship. If that attack hits, add the power die to the attack's damage roll.

entries.name: Penetrating Shot
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Weapons} When you hit a ship with a ship attack, you can expend one power die to attempt to damage another ship with the same attack. Choose a second ship within 150 feet of and directly behind your initial target. If the original {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} would hit the second ship, it takes damage equal to the number you roll on your power die. The damage is of the same type dealt by the original attack.

entries.name: Precision Shot
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Weapons} When you make a ship {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against a ship, you can expend one power die to add it to the roll. If that attack hits, add the power die to the attack's damage roll. You can use this power before or after making the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, but before any effects of the attack are applied.

entries.name: Gunning Style
entries: At 2nd rank, you adopt a particular style of gunning as your specialty. Choose one of the {@filter Gunning Styles|optionalfeatures|feature type=GS:SotG|source=sw5e-sotg} options, detailed in {@book chapter 6|sw5e-sotg|8|Chapter 6: Customization Options}. You can't take a {@filter Gunning Styles|optionalfeatures|feature type=GS:SotG|source=sw5e-sotg} option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

entries.name: {@book Improved Critical|sw5e-sotg|4|Improved Critical}
entries: Also at 2nd rank, your {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} range with primary and secondary weapons increases by 1, and when a ship rolls a 1 on a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against a tertiary or quaternary weapon that you control, they treat the effect's damage as if it had rolled the maximum.

entries.name: {@book Dependable Gunner|sw5e-sotg|4|Dependable Gunner}
entries: Starting at 3rd rank, when you roll for damage with a ship weapon, you can reroll one of the dice, but you must use the new result.  You may use this feature a number of times equal to your ranks in gunner.  You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: {@book Brutal Critical|sw5e-sotg|4|Brutal Critical}
entries: Also at 3rd rank, you can roll the weapon damage dice one additional time when determining the extra damage for a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with a ship weapon.

entries.name: Gunning Mastery
entries: At 4th rank, you master a particular style of gunning. Choose one of the {@filter Gunning Masteries|optionalfeatures|feature type=GM:SotG|source=sw5e-sotg} options, detailed in {@book chapter 6|sw5e-sotg|8|Chapter 6: Customization Options}. You can't take a {@filter Gunning Masteries|optionalfeatures|feature type=GM:SotG|source=sw5e-sotg} option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

entries.name: {@book Protean Gunner|sw5e-sotg|4|Protean Gunner}
entries: Also at 4th rank, you can choose a second {@filter Gunning Styles|optionalfeatures|feature type=GS:SotG|source=sw5e-sotg} option.

entries.name: {@book Paragon Gunner|sw5e-sotg|4|Paragon Gunner}
entries: At 5th rank, when you would expend a power die, you can use a {@dice d4} instead of expending a die. You can only use this feature once per round.

Additionally, when you make a ship {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, you can choose to make the roll a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit}. You can use this feature before or after making the roll, but before any effects of the roll are determined. Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: {@book Maximum Power|sw5e-sotg|4|Maximum Power}
entries: Also at 5th rank, when you hit a ship with a ship attack, you can deal maximum damage with that attack.
Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

{@book Dependable Tech|sw5e-sotg|4|Dependable Tech}, {@book Reroute Power|sw5e-sotg|4|Reroute Power}
{@book Rapid Repairman|sw5e-sotg|4|Rapid Repairman}, {@book Efficient Reroute|sw5e-sotg|4|Efficient Reroute}

entries.name: Venture
entries: Beginning when you choose this deployment as your specialty, at 1st rank, and again at 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th rank, you can choose a venture (see {@book chapter 6|sw5e-sotg|8|Chapter 6: Customization Options} for a list of ventures).

entries.name: {@book System Boost|sw5e-sotg|4|System Boost}
entries: Also at 1st rank, you learn techniques to quickly augment different systems on your ship that are fueled by special dice called tech dice.

entries.name: Techniques
entries: You learn two techniques of your choice, which are detailed under "Techniques" below. You can use only one technique per turn, and you can only use each technique once per round.
You learn an additional technique at 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th rank in this deployment. Each time you learn a new technique, you can also replace one technique you know with a different one.

entries.name: Tech Dice
entries: Your techniques are represented by your tech die, the starting size of which is a {@dice d4}. Using your tech die does not expend it.
Your tech die changes when you reach certain ranks in this deployment. The die becomes a {@dice d6} at 2nd rank, a {@dice d8} at 3rd rank, a {@dice d10} at 4th rank, and a {@dice d12} at 5th rank.

entries.name: Creative Thinking
entries: If you roll a 1 on your tech die, it decreases by one die size until the end of your next turn. This represents you burning through your creativity. For example, if the die is a {@dice d6} and you roll a 1, it becomes a {@dice d4}. If it’s a {@dice d4} and you roll a 1, it becomes unusable until the end of your next turn.

Conversely, if you roll the maximum number on your tech die, it increases by one die size until the end of your next turn, up to a {@dice d12}. This represents you having a creative break-through. For example, if you roll a 4 on a {@dice d4}, the die then becomes a {@dice d6}. If it's a {@dice d12} and you roll a 12, on future rolls until the end of your next turn, you can roll an extra die and choose which die to use.

entries.name: Techniques
entries: The techniques are presented in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Comms Boost
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can roll a tech die and add it to the next Charisma ({@skill Interfere|sw5e-sotg}) check your ship makes before the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Engine Tuning
entries: As an action, you can roll your tech die.  Take the result of the die and multiply it by 50. The flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} of your ship increases by this amount until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Power Distribution
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can roll your tech die and move that number of power dice from their current location to another location.

entries.name: Quiet Electronics
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can roll a tech die and add it to the next Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) check your ship makes before the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Reactor Boost
entries: As an action, you can roll your tech die.  Your reactor immediately produces that many power dice that must be stored immediately based on your ship's power coupling.  For any power dice produced in excess of your ship's capacity to store, your ship takes that many hull points in damage.

Additionally, your ship must succeed on a Constitution ({@skill Regulation|sw5e-sotg}) check (DC = 10 + the number rolled on your tech die) or take hull damage equal to one hull die + your ship's strength modifier.

entries.name: Sensor Boost
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can roll a tech die and add it to the next Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) or Intelligence ({@skill Probe|sw5e-sotg}) check your ship makes before the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Shield Reinforcement
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can roll your tech die.  Your shields immediately regenerate by the result of the die.

entries.name: Weapon Overload
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can roll your tech die.  The next time a ship weapon deals damage before the end of your next turn, it deals additional damage equal to the result of the die. The damage is of the same type dealt by the original attack.

entries.name: {@book Quick Fixer|sw5e-sotg|4|Quick Fixer}
entries: At 2nd rank, when you take the {@variantrule Patch|sw5e-sotg} action or conduct ship repairs during recharging, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the Constitution ({@skill Patch|sw5e-sotg}) check. If you already have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}, you can instead reroll one of the dice once.

entries.name: Ship Mechanic
entries: Also at 2nd rank, when installing new equipment or upgrades, you count as two members of a workforce, instead of one.

entries.name: {@book Dependable Tech|sw5e-sotg|4|Dependable Tech}
entries: Starting at 3rd rank, you can regain use of your starting tech die as a {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}.  Once you've used this feature, you must finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: {@book Reroute Power|sw5e-sotg|4|Reroute Power}
entries: Also at 3rd rank, as an action on each of your turns, you can reroute power between your ship's engines, shields, and weapons through use of the ship's power coupling. A power coupling can be toggled to neutral, where all three aspects function normally, or can divert power to a specific system.
When diverting power to a system, the effects of that system are doubled:

items: {@b Engines:} A ship's flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is doubled.
{@b Shields:} Shields take half damage and shield regeneration rate is doubled.

entries: When diverting power to a system, power to the other systems is halved:

items: {@b Engines:} A ship's flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is reduced by half.
{@b Shields:} Shields take double damage and shield regeneration rate reduced by half.
{@b Weapons:} Ship weapon damage is reduced by half.

entries.name: {@book Rapid Repairman|sw5e-sotg|4|Rapid Repairman}
entries: At 4th rank, when you take the {@variantrule Patch|sw5e-sotg} action, you can choose to forgo your proficiently equipped bonus. If you succeed on the check, you can expend 2 Hull Dice, instead of one. For each Hull Die spent in this way, roll the die and add the ship's Constitution modifier to it.

entries.name: {@book Efficient Reroute|sw5e-sotg|4|Efficient Reroute}
entries: Also at 4th rank, when you reroute power you only halve power to one other system of your choice.

entries.name: {@book Paragon Tech|sw5e-sotg|4|Paragon Tech}
entries: As of 5th tier, you are a paragon of your deployment. When you make a Strength ({@skill Boost|sw5e-sotg}) check or a Constitution (Regulate) check, you can take the maximum instead of rolling. You can use this feature before or after making the roll, but before any effects of the roll are determined. Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: {@book Supreme Boost|sw5e-sotg|4|Supreme Boost}
entries: As of 5th rank, you learn to briefly and massively boost your ship's system. When you use a technique that uses a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can use another, different technique that also uses a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} this turn. Additionally, instead of rolling your Tech die for these uses, you can choose to take the maximum.
Once you've used this feature, you must finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

rows: {@book System Disruption|sw5e-sotg|4|System Disruption}, {@book Improved Interference|sw5e-sotg|4|Improved Interference}
{@book Disrupted Defenses|sw5e-sotg|4|Disrupted Defenses}, {@book Threat Assessment|sw5e-sotg|4|Threat Assessment}
{@book Paragon Operator|sw5e-sotg|4|Paragon Operator}, {@book Overload Systems|sw5e-sotg|4|Overload Systems}

entries.name: Venture
entries: Beginning when you choose this deployment as your specialty, at 1st rank, and again at 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th rank, you can choose a venture (see {@book chapter 6|sw5e-sotg|8|Chapter 6: Customization Options} for a list of ventures).

entries.name: {@book Operational Control|sw5e-sotg|4|Operational Control}
entries: Also at 1st rank, you learn disruptions that are fueled by special dice called power dice.

entries.name: Disruptions
entries: You learn two disruptions of your choice, which are detailed under "Disruptions" below. You can use only one disruption per turn, and you can only use each disruption once per round.
You learn an additional disruption at 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th rank in this deployment. Each time you learn a new disruption, you can also replace one disruption you know with a different one.

entries.name: Power Dice
entries: A power die is expended when you use it. Your ship must have a power die at the required system in order to use the disruption.

Your ship gains power dice based primarily on reactor production.  These power dice are stored in a central and/or system capacitors to power abilities of crewmembers.  Your power die type is determined by your ship tier.

entries.name: Saving Throws
entries: Some of your Disruptions require your target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the disruption's effects. The {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC is calculated as follows:
{@b Disruption save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your ship's Charisma modifier

entries.name: Disruptions
entries: The collaborations are presented in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Enhance Scopes
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Sensors} As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, can expend one power die to increase the ranges of your ship's next primary or secondary {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} by 500 feet. If it hits, you add the power die to the attack’s damage roll.

entries.name: Disarming Shot
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Sensors} As an action, you can expend one power die to attempt to disarm the target. You add the power die to your ship's next {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}.  On a hit, in addition to the normal damage taken, the target must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, you disable a weapon of the target ship of your choice until the ship recharges.

entries.name: Hacked Communications
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Comms} As an action, you may expend a power die, and choose any number of ships that you can see within 600 feet of you. Each ship must succeed on a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or take ionic damage equal to the number rolled on the die + your ship's Charisma modifier (minimum of one). Additionally, on a failed save, the ship's communication devices are {@condition Disabled|sw5e-sotg|disabled} until rebooted.

entries.name: Reactor Vulnerability
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Comms} When a friendly ship, including your own, hits a ship with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}, you can expend a superiority die as a {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to temporarily destabilize the ship's reactor. Add the number rolled to the damage of the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} and the ship must succeed on a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be {@condition Shocked|sw5e-sotg|shocked} until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Remote Sensors
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Sensors} Whenever you make a Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) or an Intelligence ({@skill Probe|sw5e-sotg}) check, you can employ the aid of remote sensors by expending a power die, adding the number rolled to the check. You can use this maneuver before or after making the {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, but before the results of the {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} are determined.

entries.name: Sensor Blast
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Comms} When a friendly ship, including your own, hits a target with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}, you can expend one power die as a {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to attempt to saturate the target's sensors. You add the power die to the attack’s damage roll, and the target must make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on all {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against targets other than your ship until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Systems Block
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Comms} When a friendly ship, including yuor own, makes an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and expend a power die and add it to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}. On a hit, the target’s next attack has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} and it cannot regain shield points until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Targeted Strike
entries: {@i {@b Power Die Location:} Sensors} When a friendly ship, including your own, makes an attack against a target, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to expend a power die. You add the power die to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, and the damage roll if it hits. You can use this maneuver before or after the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, but before the GM determines whether or not the attack hits.

entries.name: System Disturbance
entries: At 2nd rank, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can choose a ship that you can see within 1,000 feet and target its systems for disturbance. For the next minute, or until you disturb another target, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on any Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) or Intelligence ({@skill Probe|sw5e-sotg}) check you make to find it.

Additionally, when the ship makes an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to disturb the ship's functions. Roll a System Disturbance die, which is a {@dice d6}, and subtract it from the {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. You can choose to use this feature after the ship makes its roll, but before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. You can use this feature twice. You gain another use of this feature at 3rd, 4th, and 5th rank in this deployment. You regain any expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
Your System Disturbance die changes when you reach certain ranks in this deployment. The die becomes a {@dice d8} at 3rd rank, a {@dice d10} at 4th rank, and a {@dice d12} at 5th rank.

entries.name: {@book Improved Interference|sw5e-sotg|4|Improved Interference}
entries: Also at 2nd rank, when you take the {@variantrule Interfere|sw5e-sotg} action, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the Charisma ({@skill Interfere|sw5e-sotg}) check. If you already have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}, you can instead reroll one of the dice once.

entries.name: Disturbed Defenses
entries: At 3rd rank, the first time the target of your System Disturbance takes damage each round, it takes additional damage equal to your System Disturbance die. The damage is of the same type dealt by the original attack.

entries.name: {@book Threat Assessment|sw5e-sotg|4|Threat Assessment}
entries: Also at 3rd rank, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can learn certain information about the capabilities of the target of your System Disturbance. The GM tells you if the ship is your ship's equal, superior, or inferior in regard to two of the following characteristics of your choice:

items: Current total hull and shield points

entries.name: {@book Masterful Interference|sw5e-sotg|4|Masterful Interference}
entries: At 4th rank, when you take the {@variantrule Interfere|sw5e-sotg} action, you can choose to forgo your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. If you succeed on the check, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on all {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} or {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} it makes before the start of your next turn, instead of one.

entries.name: {@book Haywire|sw5e-sotg|4|Haywire}
entries: Also at 4th rank, when you target a ship with your System Disturbance feature, it must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to Interfere checks). On a failed save, while it is the target of your System Disturbance feature, the first time it makes an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} or a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} each round, the target must roll a {@dice d4} and subtract the number rolled from the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

entries.name: {@book Paragon Operator|sw5e-sotg|4|Paragon Operator}
entries: As of 5th rank, you are a paragon of your deployment. When you would expend a Power die or a System Disturbance die, you can use a {@dice d4} instead of expending a die. You can only use this feature once per round.
Additionally, you regain all expended uses of your System Disturbance feature when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

Lastly, when you would make an Interfere, Scan, or Probe check, you can take the maximum instead of rolling. You can use this feature before or after making the roll, but before any effects of the roll are determined. Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: {@book Overload Systems|sw5e-sotg|4|Overload Systems}
entries: Also at 5th rank, you learn how to overload the systems of a ship remotely. As an action, you can attempt to breach the systems of the target of your System Disturbance. The ship must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to Interfere checks). On a failed save, the target's flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} reduced by half, it's turning {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is doubled, it takes a -2 penalty to AC and Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}, it's shields no longer regenerate, and it can't use reactions. On its turn, it can use either an action or a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, not both. Regardless of the ship's abilities, crew, or equipment, it can't make more than one attack during its turn.
The ship's pilot makes another Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} at the end of its turns. On a successful save, the effect ends.
Once you've use this feature, you must finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.
