Tiny ships rarely have a hyperdrive, while Small ships occasionally do. Medium and larger ships typically have a hyperdrive.

The {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} of a hyperdrive is rated on an inverse scale: the faster the hyperdrive, the lower the rating or "Class". Acting as a multiplier for a given base travel time then, a Class 2 hyperdrive takes twice the base time to travel a given route, while the Millennium Falcon's Class 0.5 takes only half the base time.

A ship can have multiple hyperdrives. Larger ships typically have a back-up in case of failure. Only one hyperdrive can be activated at a time. Your ship must have a hyperdrive slot for each hyperdrive.

entries.name: Docking
entries: All starships require refueling and restocking, as well as a place to dock where they can get these services.

entries.name: Docking Fees
entries: Docking fees vary planet-to-planet, but typically average around 20 credits per day in an average spaceport for a Tiny or Small ship. For a Medium or larger ship, multiply the amount by the {@b Starship Size Equipment Cost} table.

For Large and larger ships, docking on planet is impractical. Typically, most civilized planets will have docking station in space that the characters can dock to. Alternatively, if they don't need to refuel or restock, they can simply remain in orbit and bypass any docking fees, while the party themselves transfer to the planet's surface in a smaller transport.

entries.name: Long Term Storage
entries: Long-term storage is available in some locations, averaging around 200 credits per month for a Tiny or Small ship. For a Medium or larger ship, multiply the amount by the {@b Starship Size Equipment Cost} table.
Again, it is impractical for a Large or larger ship to to be stored on planet. At large shipyards, long term storage might be available.
It generally requires about eight hours to get a ship out of long-term storage and ready for flight.

entries.name: Refueling and Restocking
entries: All ships require fuel to operate; without it, a ship is effectively {@condition Disabled|sw5e-sotg|disabled}. In general, most starships refuel each time they put into port, and during refueling other essential ship consumables (such as water and oxygen) are restocked as well.

entries.name: Refueling
entries: Ships consume fuel in terms of "units", the quantity of which varies by the size of the ship. A ship uses a unit's worth of fuel for one day of flight in realspace or hyperspace, after one hour of flight in atmosphere, or in a single jump to hyperspeed. Costs for a unit's worth of fuel can be found below on the {@b Starship Size Fuel Cost} table.

entries.name: Starship Size Fuel Cost
entries: Additionally, a ship can store an amount of fuel, as determined by its size, in the {@b Starship Size Fuel Capacity} table below.

entries.name: Primary Systems
entries: When a ship refuels, their primary systems, such as electricity and life support, are also replenished. As long the starship has fuel remaining, primary systems function.

entries.name: Restocking
entries: Ships store food and beverage in terms of "portions", the quantity of which varies by the size of the ship. Each living creature aboard a ship consumes one portion per day spent aboard the ship. A portion costs 10 credits.

data.name: Chapter 6: Customization Options
entries: The combination of your character's personal   features, as well as their chosen deployment, defines your character's capabilities in the space component of the game, and the personal details you create set your character apart from every other character. Even within your class, species, and deployment specialization you have options to fine-tune what your character can do. But this chapter is for players who want to go a step further.

This chapter defines two sets of rules for customizing your character: multispeccing and ventures. Multispeccing lets you combine deployments together, and ventures are special options you can choose as you gain ranks.
Ships are locked to their respective size-driven tiers and have no multiclass parallels.

entries.name: Multispecializing
entries: Multispecializing allows you to gain ranks in multiple deployment specializations. Doing so lets you mix the abilities of those deployments to realize a character concept that might not be reflected in one of the standard specialization options.

With this rule, you have the option of gaining a rank in a new specialization whenever you advance in rank, instead of gaining a rank in your current specialization. Your ranks in all your deployments are added together to determine your character rank. For example, if you have two ranks in pilot and one in gunner, you're a 3rd-rank character.

As you advance in ranks, you might primarily remain a member of your original deployment with just a single rank in another specialization, or you might change course entirely, never looking back at the deployment you left behind. You might even start progressing in a third or fourth specialization. Compared to a single-specialized character of the same rank, you'll sacrifice some focus in exchange for versatility.

entries.name: Multispecializing Example
entries: Drew is playing a 1st-rank pilot. When his character is ready to progress to 2nd rank, Drew decides that his character will multispec instead of continuing to progress as a pilot. Drew's character has been spending a lot of time with Rickey's gunner, and has even been doing some simulations. Drew decides that his character will multispec into the gunner deployment, and thus his character becomes a 1st-rank pilot and 1st-rank gunner (written as pilot 1/gunner 1). When Drew's character is ready to progress to 3rd rank, he can decide whether to add another pilot rank (becoming a pilot 2/gunner 1), another gunner rank (becoming a pilot 1/gunner 2), or a rank in a third deployment, perhaps dabbling in the inner workings of the ship (becoming a pilot 1/gunner 1/mechanic 1).

entries.name: Prerequisites
entries: Unlike classes, there are no requirements for multispeccing. When a player has progressed to a rank higher than 1, they can choose to multispec or focus on their primary deployment specialization, with no external requirements or considerations.

entries.name: Milestones
entries: Rather than traditional experience and book-keeping, ranks should be awarded as milestones for completing a specific encounter, or obtaining certain knowledge.

entries.name: Proficiency Bonus
entries: Ships do not have a {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. When a feature references a {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, instead use the {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} of the appropriate crewmember as long as the crewmember has at least one deployment rank.

Rather than having a separate {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} for the space and ground portions of your game, your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} for space is the same as that of the ground.
If a deployment feature or venture allows you to forgo your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, you may only do so once.

entries.name: Expertise
entries: If you have {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in a skill as well as a feature that lets you forgo your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, you can only forgo your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} once. For instance, if you are a 5th-level, 4th-rank pilot with an 18 in Intelligence and {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in {@skill Piloting|sw5e-phb}, you add 10 to your {@skill Piloting|sw5e-phb} checks (4 + 2 x 3). If you use the 4th-rank pilot feature "{@book That's a Good Trick|sw5e-sotg|4|That's a Good Trick}" to forgo your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, you instead add 7 for the {@skill Piloting|sw5e-phb} check as a part of that Evade action (4 + 2 x 3 - 3).

entries.name: Gunning Styles
entries: Certain deployment features or ventures offer your choice of {@filter Gunning Styles|optionalfeatures|feature type=GS:SotG|source=sw5e-sotg}. Choose from the following. You can't take a {@filter Gunning Styles|optionalfeatures|feature type=GS:SotG|source=sw5e-sotg} option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

entries.name: Cannoneer
entries: {@optfeature Cannoneer|sw5e-sotg}
You are skilled with laser cannons. While you are firing a primary weapon, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls and save DCs.

entries.name: Heavy Gunner
entries: {@optfeature Heavy Gunner|sw5e-sotg}
You are skilled with railguns and turbolasers. While you are firing a secondary weapon, you gain a +2 bonus to {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} and save DCs.

entries.name: Payload Delivery
entries: {@optfeature Payload Delivery|sw5e-sotg}

You are skilled with mines, missiles, rockets, and other explosive weapons. When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for a tertiary or quaternary weapon, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll, even if the new roll is a 1 or a 2.

entries.name: Gunning Masteries
entries: Certain deployment features or ventures offer your choice of {@filter Gunning Masteries|optionalfeatures|feature type=GM:SotG|source=sw5e-sotg}. Choose from the following. You can't take a {@filter Gunning Masteries|optionalfeatures|feature type=GM:SotG|source=sw5e-sotg} option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

entries.name: Cannon Mastery
entries: {@optfeature Cannon Mastery|sw5e-sotg}

You are the master of laser cannons. While you are firing a primary weapon, when you take the {@variantrule Fire|sw5e-sotg} action, you can choose to fire rapidly at the expense of accuracy. Your attacks are made without the aid of your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, but you use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to make an additional attack, also without your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Heavy Gun Mastery
entries: {@optfeature Heavy Gun Mastery|sw5e-sotg}

You are the master of railguns and turbolasers. While you are firing a secondary weapon, before you make an attack, you can choose to double your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. If the attack hits, you reduce the damage dealt by an amount equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Payload Mastery
entries: {@optfeature Payload Mastery|sw5e-sotg}

You are the master of missiles, rockets, and other ship-board explosive weapons. While you are firing a tertiary or quaternary weapon, you can choose to reduce the DC by an amount equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. If you do, and the target fails the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, they take additional damage equal to twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Ventures
entries: Ventures represent talents beyond the deployment specialization of a character. This embodies their training and experience in other aspects of their lives. At certain deployment ranks, your deployment gives you the Venture feature. You can take each venture only once, unless the venture's description says otherwise.

You must meet any prerequisite specified in a venture to take that venture. If you ever lose a venture's prerequisite, you can't use that venture again until you regain the prerequisite. For example, the Spacecasting venture requires you to be able to cast force or {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. If your character loses the ability to do so, you can't benefit from the Spacecasting venture until you regain the ability to cast force or {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

Ventures, and this book in general, are designed and written in such a way that they have minimal impact on the ground game. All ventures are intended to only be usable while deployed aboard a ship, even if they don't explicitly say it.

entries.name: Analytical Coordinator
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 1 level in scholar} When an ally makes an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} or {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} affected by your Direct action, and they are also the target of your Critical Analysis class feature, they can also roll a {@dice d6} and add it to the {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} or {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}.

entries.name: Astrogation Mechanic
entries: When you make an Intelligence ({@skill Astrogation|sw5e-sotg}) check, your ship is considered proficiently equipped if you have proficiency in {@skill Technology|sw5e-phb} or expertly equipped if you have {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in {@skill Technology|sw5e-phb}.

Additionally, when you make a Constitution ({@skill Patch|sw5e-sotg}) check when taking the Patch action, your ship is considered proficiently equipped if you have proficiency in {@item Mechanic's kit|sw5e-phb|Mechanic's Kit} or expertly equipped if you have {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in {@item Mechanic's kit|sw5e-phb|Mechanic's Kit}.

entries.name: Calculating Gunner
entries: When you make an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with a secondary ship weapon, you can use your Intelligence modifier, instead of the ship's Wisdom modifier, for the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}.

entries.name: Counterslicer
entries: When you are the target of the Interfere action and are forced to make an Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}), if you succeed on the contest, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the next Charisma ({@skill Interfere|sw5e-sotg}) check you make before the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Cunning Operator
entries: When you take the {@variantrule Interfere|sw5e-sotg} action and fail the contest, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to repeat the check against the same target.

entries.name: Diamond Deployment
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 14 levels in monk} While deployed, when your ship fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can spend 1 focus point to reroll the die.

entries.name: Dogfighter Superiority
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 2 levels in fighter} When you expend a power die or another die granted by your Deployment, roll the die as normal, but you can instead subtract it from your pool of {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}.

entries.name: Experienced Slicer
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:}  at least 1 rank in operator} When setting your Operator's Disruptions save DC and whenever a Disruption uses your ship's Charisma modifier, you may add half your Intelligence modifier.

entries.name: Explosive Gambits
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 3 ranks in gunner} Once per turn, when you roll the maximum on a gambit die, you can roll an additional die and add it to the roll.

entries.name: Flurry of Fire
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 2 levels in monk} Immediately after you take the {@variantrule Fire|sw5e-sotg} action you can spend 1 focus point to make an additional attack as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}. This additional attack must be made with a primary weapon.

entries.name: Force-Empowered Accuracy
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 2 levels in consular} Once per turn, when you miss with a ship attack, or when a target succeeds on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against a ship weapon, you can spend 1 force point to reroll the die. You must use the new roll.

entries.name: Force-Empowered Blasting
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 2 levels in guardian} Once per turn, when you deal damage with a ship weapon, you can spend 1 force point to deal an additional 1d8 damage to the target. The damage is the same type as the weapon's damage.

entries.name: Force-Empowered Shooting
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 2 levels in sentinel} When you take the {@variantrule Fire|sw5e-sotg} action, you can spend 1 force point to make an additional attack with a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}. This additional attack must be made with a primary weapon.

entries.name: Force Piloting
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} The ability to cast {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}} When you make an Dexterity (Manuever) check while aboard your ship, you may add half (round up) your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice), to your result. Additionally, you can add half (round up) your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice) to your ship's AC while at the helm.

entries.name: Force Purification
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 14 levels in guardian} Ships become valid targets for you Cleansing Touch ability.

entries.name: Furious Gunner
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 1 level in berserker} While raging and firing a primary weapon, you can take a penalty to your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} up to your rage damage bonus, adding twice the amount to the damage roll on a hit.

entries.name: Gunner Adept
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Rank 2} You have gunner training that allows you to perform special combat gambits. You learn two gambits of your choice from among those available to the gunner deployment.

entries.name: Gunning Mastery
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Rank 5} You master a particular style of gunning. Choose one of the {@filter Gunning Masteries|optionalfeatures|feature type=GM:SotG|source=sw5e-sotg} options, detailed above. You can select this venture multiple times. You can't take a {@filter Gunning Masteries|optionalfeatures|feature type=GM:SotG|source=sw5e-sotg} option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

entries.name: Gunning Stylist
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Rank 3} You adopt a particular style of gunning as your specialty. Choose one of the {@filter Gunning Styles|optionalfeatures|feature type=GS:SotG|source=sw5e-sotg} options options, detailed above. You can select this venture multiple times. You can't take a {@filter Gunning Styles|optionalfeatures|feature type=GS:SotG|source=sw5e-sotg} option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

entries.name: Hot Wire
entries: When you would make a Constitution ({@skill Patch|sw5e-sotg}) check while aboard your ship, you can instead make an Intelligence ({@item Mechanic's kit|sw5e-phb|Mechanic's Kit}).

entries.name: Indomitable Starship
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 9 levels in fighter} While deployed, when your ship fails a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can use your Indomitable class feature to reroll the die.

entries.name: Infiltration
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 10 levels in scout} You can take the Fly or Conceal actions as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on each of your turns.

When you attempt to Conceal your ship, you can opt to not move your ship more than half its {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} on that turn. If you do so, ships that attempt to detect you take a -10 penalty to their Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) checks until the start of your next turn. You lose this benefit if you move more than half your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, either voluntarily or because of some external effect. You are still automatically detected if any effect or action causes you to no longer be hidden.
If you are still hidden on your next turn, you can continue to move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} and gain this benefit until you are detected.
Finally, you can no longer be tracked by unenhanced means, unless you choose to leave a trail.

entries.name: Infuse Ship Weapon
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 2 levels in engineer} Ship weapons become valid targets for your Infuse Item class feature.

entries.name: Intuitive Gunner
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} The ability to cast {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}} When you determine the save DC for a tertiary ship weapon while on a Medium or smaller ship, you can add half your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice) to the save DC.

entries.name: Keen Eye
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Rank 4} When you take the {@action Search|sw5e-phb} action and succeed on a Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) or Intelligence ({@skill Probe|sw5e-sotg}) check aided by your ship's scanners, you can learn certain information about a target if you are aware of them. The GM tells you if the ship is your ship's equal, superior, or inferior in regard to one of the following characteristics of your choice:

items: Current total hull and shield points
Current shield die type and number, and shield regeneration rate

entries: Once you've targeted a ship with this feature, you can't target it again until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Lock on Target
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} The ability to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}} {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 1 rank in gunner} Once per turn, when you hit a target with a ship attack from a primary or secondary weapon, you may use a {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to spend one tech point to mark the target. The next {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} you make against the ship before the end of your next turn can’t suffer from {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

entries.name: Multi-Roled
entries: When you take Dual Role, choose a secondary deployment. When you advance a rank in your primary deployment, you may select a deployment maneuver (collaboration, gambit, technique, disruption, tactic, or stratagem) from your secondary deployment instead of your primary deployment.
If your chosen secondary deployment is Mechanic, you can use a power die from any location instead of a tech die for that technique.

entries.name: Multi-Roled, Improved
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:}  Multi-Roled} When you advance a rank in your primary deployment, you may select a deployment maneuver (collaboration, gambit, technique, disruption, tactic, or stratagem) from any deployment instead of your primary deployment.
If your chosen maneuver is a technique, you can use a power die from any location instead of a tech die for that technique.

entries.name: Multi-Rolled, Legendary
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:}  Dual Roles, Multi-Roles, Rank 5} Over a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} you may switch out a number of deployment maneuvers (collaboration, gambit, technique, disruption, tactic, or stratagem) you know up to your intelligence modifier (minimum of 1) for an equal number of maneuvers from other deployments.
If any of your chosen maneuvers are a technique, you can use a power die from any location instead of a tech die for that technique.

entries.name: Multitasker
entries: When operating a ship, you gain a second {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} you can take with the ship.

entries.name: Multitasker, Improved
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Multitasker} When operating a ship, you gain a second {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} you can take with the ship.

entries.name: Multitasker, Legendary
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:}  Multitasker, Improved; Rank 5} When operating a ship, you gain a second action you can take with the ship.

entries.name: Natural Slicer
entries: Whenever you make a Charisma ({@skill Interfere|sw5e-sotg}) check, you may instead make an Intelligence (Slicer Tools) check.

entries.name: Perceptive Techie
entries: When you make a Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) or Intelligence ({@skill Probe|sw5e-sotg}) check while aboard your ship, you may use your Wisdom modifier instead of your ship's Ability modifier.

entries.name: Persistent Interference
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 3 ranks in operator} When you take the {@variantrule Interfere|sw5e-sotg} action and succeed on the contest, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the next Charisma ({@skill Interfere|sw5e-sotg}) check before the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Pilot Adept
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Rank 2} You have pilot training that allows you to perform special combat tactics. You learn two tactics of your choice from among those available to the Pilot deployment.

entries.name: Pilot in Training
entries: When you make a Dexterity ({@skill Maneuvering|sw5e-sotg}) check while at the helm, you can add your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} to checks you make if you do not already do so.

entries.name: Precision GUNNER
entries: When you make an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with a primary ship weapon while on a Large or smaller ship, you can use your Dexterity modifier, instead of the ship's Wisdom modifier, for the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}.

entries.name: Protected by the Force
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 3 levels in consular} When your ship is hit by an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to shroud your ship in Force energy. Until the start of your next turn, you have a bonus to AC equal to your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of +1). This includes the triggering attack.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, as shown in the consular table. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Reckless Ramming
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 2 levels in berserker} When you take the {@variantrule Ram|sw5e-sotg} action, you can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the Dexterity ({@skill Maneuvering|sw5e-sotg}) check, and you deal additional damage equal to your rage damage bonus. The first {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} made against your ship before the start of your next turn has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}.

entries.name: Recurrent Repairs
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 3 ranks in mechanic} When you succeed on a Constitution ({@skill Patch|sw5e-sotg}) check as a part of a Patch action you take, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the next Constitution ({@skill Patch|sw5e-sotg}) check you take as a part of the Patch action you take before the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Resourceful Display
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 1 rank in coordinator} Once per round, when you, or an ally with your {@book Inspiring Display|sw5e-sotg|4|Inspiring Display} die, roll an {@book Inspiring Display|sw5e-sotg|4|Inspiring Display}, they can roll the die twice and take either result.

entries.name: Resourceful Gambits
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 1 rank in gunner} Once per round, when you roll a power die used for a gunner's gambit, you can roll the die twice and take either result.

entries.name: Resourceful Boost
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 1 rank in mechanic} Once per round, when you use your {@book System Boost|sw5e-sotg|4|System Boost} feature, you can roll the tech die twice and take either result.

entries.name: Resourceful Disruption
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 1 rank in operator} Once per round, when you roll a power die as part of an operator's disruption, you can roll the die twice and take either result.

entries.name: Resourceful Tactics
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 1 rank in pilot} Once per round, when you roll a power die as part of a pilot's tactic, you can roll the die twice and take either result.

entries.name: Resourceful Technician
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 1 rank in technician} Once per round, when you roll a power die as part of a technician's stratagem, you can roll the die twice and take either result.

entries.name: Scanner Specialist
entries: When you take the {@action Search|sw5e-phb} action, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) and Intelligence ({@skill Probe|sw5e-sotg}) checks that rely on the scanner.

entries.name: Shield Tweaker
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} The Ability to Cast 1st level Tech Powers} If your ship has 1 or more shield points remaining, as a {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to your ship taking damage, you may spend two tech points to tweak your ship's shields to capture some of the incoming energy, lessening its effect on your ship and storing it for your ship's next primary {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}. Your ship gains resistance to the triggering damage type until the start of your ship's next turn. Also, the first time your ship hits with a primary {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} on your ship's next turn, the target takes an extra 1d6 damage of the triggering type, and the power ends.

entries.name: Shrewd Interrogator
entries: When you make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}) or Charisma ({@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}) check while aboard your ship, you may use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Wisdom or Charisma modifier.

entries.name: Slippery Pilot
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 2 levels in operative} Your quick thinking and agility allow you to act and move your ship quickly. You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on each of your turns in combat. This action can be used only to take the Conceal, Evade, or Fly action.

entries.name: Sneak Firing
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 1 level in operative} Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one ship you hit with a ship attack if you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}.  You can select this venture multiple times.

entries.name: Spacecasting
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} The ability to cast force or {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}} When casting a force or {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} while aboard your ship and in space, the power's range is multiplied by 2. You can not target a hostile creature with a power unless you are aware of their presence and location.

entries.name: Spacecasting, Greater
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Spacecasting, Improved} When casting a force or {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} while aboard your ship and in space, the power's range is instead multiplied by 100. You can not target a hostile creature with a power unless you are aware of their presence and location.
Additionally, when casting a force or {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} while aboard your ship and in space that affects an area, the area's dimensions are instead multiplied by 10.
Lastly, when casting a force or {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} while aboard your ship and in space, you instead divide by 5 when scaling damage against Tiny ships.

entries.name: Spacecasting, Improved
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Spacecasting} When casting a force or {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} while aboard your ship and in space, the power's range is instead multiplied by 10. You can not target a hostile creature with a power unless you are aware of their presence and location.
Additionally, when casting a force or {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} while aboard your ship and in space that affects an area, the area's dimensions are multiplied by 2.

entries.name: Spacecasting, Legendary
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Spacecasting, Master} When casting a force or {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} while aboard your ship and in space that affects an area, the area's dimensions are instead multiplied by 1,000.
Additionally, when casting a force or {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} while aboard your ship and in space, you ignore the damage scaling against Medium and smaller ships.

entries.name: Spacecasting, Master
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Spacecasting, Greater} When casting a force or {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} while aboard your ship and in space, the power's range is instead multiplied by 1,000. You can not target a hostile creature with a power unless you are aware of their presence and location.
Additionally, when casting a force or {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} while aboard your ship and in space that affects an area, the area's dimensions are instead multiplied by 100.
Lastly, when casting a force or {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} while aboard your ship and in space, you instead divide by 2 when scaling damage against Small and smaller ships.

entries.name: Space Explorer
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 1 level in scout} While deployed, parts of your Skilled Explorer class feature extend to your ship:

items: Your ship is not {@condition Slowed|sw5e-sotg|slowed} by {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain}.
Your ship can't get lost by unenhanced means.
Your ship can move stealthily at a normal pace.

entries.name: Storming Gunner
entries: You can use your immense strength to steady primary weapons with the burst, rapid, or saturate features.  When you make an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with a primary ship weapon having at least one of these features while on a Medium or smaller ship, you can use your Strength modifier, instead of the ship's Wisdom modifier, for the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} or setting the DC for the targets' saves.

entries.name: Strong Alone, Stronger Together
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 3 ranks in coordinator} When you take the {@variantrule Direct|sw5e-sotg} action, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the next {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} you make before the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Tactical Superiority
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 2 levels in scholar} When you expend a power die or another die granted by a Deployment, roll the die as normal, but you can instead subtract it from your pool of {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}.

entries.name: TARGETING FIRE
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 1 rank in gunner} When you take this {@book Venture|sw5e-sotg|8|Ventures}, you may select two areas that you are adept at targeting.  You may take this Venture multiple times.  Each time you do so, you may select two additional target areas.

Once per turn, when you hit a target with a ship attack from a primary or secondary weapon, you may use a {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to either forego {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} if you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}, spend one tech point, or spend one force point to target a specific area of the ship causing targeted damage there:

entries.name: ENGINES
entries: The target gain 1 {@condition Slowed|sw5e-sotg} Level until the end of its turn as it suffers damage to its engines.

entries.name: Fire Control System
entries: You damage the target's targeting systems.  The first time the target forces you to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} before the start of your next turn, the target takes an additional 1d6 ionic damage, and you can roll 1d4 and add the number rolled to your {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

entries.name: Gravity Generator
entries: You cause each Large or smaller ship within 100 feet of the target to make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your ship's Strength modifier).  On a failure, that ship is pulled to the nearest unoccupied space adjacent to the target.

entries.name: Reactor
entries: You destabilize the ship's reactor. Until the start of your next turn, if the target becomes {@condition Tractored|sw5e-sotg|tractored}, {@condition Ionized|sw5e-sotg|ionized}, or {@condition Shocked|sw5e-sotg|shocked}, the reactor suffers damaging feedback, causing the ship to immediately take 1d8 ionic damage.

entries.name: Sensors
entries: You create an illusory duplicate of your ship in your space that only the target can see. The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the next {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} it makes against your ship before the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Shields
entries: You cause the target to take additional damage to the target's shields equal to your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} modifier at the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Static Discharge Vanes
entries: You cause the target to become {@condition Shocked|sw5e-sotg|shocked} until the end of your ship's next turn. When this attack hits a target, if there is a ship within 300 feet who is {@condition Shocked|sw5e-sotg|shocked}, an arc of lightning courses between the two ships, dealing 1d6 lightning damage to both of them. If there are multiple other ships who are {@condition Shocked|sw5e-sotg|shocked}, the lightning leaps to the closest ship.

entries.name: Weapons
entries: You damage the ship's weapon systems.  The first time it would deal damage before the start of your next turn, that damage is reduced by 1d6.

entries.name: GM Note:
entries: If a ship being fought does not have the system that is targeted in the Targeting Fire venture (e.g., an X-Wing hit by an attack utilizing Targeting Fire: Gravity Generator does not have a gravity generator), then consider allowing the venture's effects to work via alternative means (e.g., the hyperdrive is hit instead).

entries.name: Technological Knowledge
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 3 levels in engineer} Ships become a valid target of your potent aptitude ability.

entries.name: Thread the Needle
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 3 ranks in pilot} When you take the Evade action, you can gain the benefits of Evade against only a single target in order to avoid the penalty of {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on any skill check or {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} made by your ship or anyone on it.

entries.name: Trust in the Force
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} at least 10 levels in sentinel} When you take the Dogfight action, you can make a Dexterity ({@skill Maneuvering|sw5e-sotg}) check (DC = 10 + the number of enemy ships you can see).  On a success, the next attack made against your ship by any ship you can see is not granted {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} by the Dogfight action.

entries.name: Weapon Enhancement
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} The ability to cast 3rd level {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}} As an action, you may touch an unenhanced ship weapon on your ship and spend four tech points, making it an enhanced weapon, for up to an hour, as long as you maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}. Additionally, choose one of these damage types: acid, cold, energy, fire, ion, kinetic, or lightning.  The unenhanced ship weapon you touch has a +1 to {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} and deals an extra 1d4 damage of the chosen type for the duration.

entries.name: Weapon Overheat
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} The ability to cast 2nd level {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}} As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you may spend three tech points to empower a ship weapon on your ship. For up to an hour, as long as you maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}, you can cool the weapon once per turn without using an action, and as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on each of your turns you can make one attack with the weapon.

data.name: Chapter 7: Using Ability Scores
entries: Six abilities provide a quick description of every ship's, physical and electronic characteristics:

items: {@b Intelligence}, measuring processing and data storage
{@b Wisdom}, measuring targeting, sensors, and awareness
{@b Charisma}, measuring presence and electronic communications power and ability

entries: Is a ship tough, and her crew well-trained? Fast and frightening? Nimble and notorious? Ability scores de-fine these traits—a ship's strengths and weaknesses.

The three main rolls of the game-the {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}-rely on the six ability scores. The book's introduction describes the basic rule behind these rolls: roll a {@dice d20}, add an ability modifier derived from one of the six ability scores, and compare the total to a target number.

This chapter focuses on how to use {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}, covering the fundamental activities that creatures attempt in the game. Rules for {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} appear in chapter 9.

entries.name: Ability Scores and Modifiers
entries: Each of a ship's abilities has a score, a number that defines the magnitude of that ability. An ability score is not just a measure of innate capabilities, but also encompasses a ship's modification, in activities related to that ability.

A score of 10 or 11 is the normal average, but many ships are a cut above average in most abilities. A score of 18 is the highest that a ship usually reaches. Some can have scores as high as 20, and monsters and capital ships can have scores as high as 30.

Each ability also has a modifier, derived from the score and ranging from -5 (for an ability score of 1) to +10 (for a score of 30). The Ability Scores and Modifiers table notes the ability modifiers for the range of possible ability scores, from 1 to 30.
To determine an ability modifier without consulting the table, subtract 10 from the ability score and then divide the total by 2 (round down).

Because ability modifiers affect almost every {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, ability modifiers come up in play more often than their associated scores.

entries.name: Advantage and Disadvantage
entries: Sometimes a special ability or power tells you that you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} or {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, or an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}. When that happens, you roll a second {@dice d20} when you make the roll. Use the higher of the two rolls if you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}, and use the lower roll if you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}. For example, if you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} and roll a 17 and a 5, you use the 5. If you instead have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} and roll those numbers, you use the 17.

If multiple situations affect a roll and each one grants {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} or imposes {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on it, you don't roll more than one additional {@dice d20}. If two favorable situations grant {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}, for example, you still roll only one additional {@dice d20}.

If circumstances cause a roll to have both {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} and {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}, you are considered to have neither of them, and you roll one {@dice d20}. This is true even if multiple circumstances impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} and only one grants {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} or vice versa. In such a situation, you have neither {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} nor {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

When you make a roll with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} or {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}, only the {@dice d20} is rolled twice. Any additional dice, such as the {@dice d4} granted by the {@i guidance} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, are only rolled once.

When you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} or {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} and something in the game, such as the iktotchi's Precognition trait, lets you reroll the {@dice d20}, you can reroll only one of the dice. You choose which one. For example, if an iktotchi has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} and rolls a 1 and a 13, the iktotchi could use the Precognition trait to reroll the 1.

You usually gain {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} or {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} through the use of special abilities, actions, or powers. Inspiration (see chapter 4) can also give a character {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on checks related to the character's personality, ideals, or bonds. The GM can also decide that circumstances influence a roll in one direction or the other and grant {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} or impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} as a result.

entries.name: Advantage on Other Rolls
entries: Though less common, {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} and {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} can occur on other types of rolls as well. When you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} or {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on a roll, as with a {@dice d20}, you roll the dice twice, using the higher of the two results with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}, and using the lower of the two results if you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}. If a roll has multiple dice, you roll the dice together and treat the results separately.

For instance, the Boost Weapons action potentially grants {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on a ship damage roll once per turn. If any additional dice would be added to the damage roll, those additional dice are only rolled once.

entries.name: Proficiently Equipped
entries: Ships can be proficiently equipped for particular tasks, allowing her crew to add their {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} to the roll or save, as long as the crewmember has at least one deployment rank. Enemy ships also have this bonus, which is incorporated in their stat blocks. The bonus is used in the rules on {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks}, {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}, and {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}.

Your proficiency equipped bonus can't be added to a single die roll or other number more than once. For example, if two different rules say you can add your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} to a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you nevertheless add the bonus only once when you make the save.

Occasionally, your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} might be multiplied or divided (doubled or halved, for example) before you apply it. If a circumstance suggests that your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} applies more than once to the same roll, you still add it only once and multiply or divide it only once.

By the same token, if a feature or effect allows you to multiply your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} when making an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} that wouldn't normally benefit from your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, you still don't add the bonus to the check. For that check your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} is 0, given the fact that multiplying 0 by any number is still 0. For instance, if you are not proficiently equipped in the Data skill, you gain no benefit from a feature that lets you double your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} when you make Intelligence ({@skill Data|sw5e-sotg}) checks.

In general, you don't multiply your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} for {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. If a feature or effect allows you to do so, these same rules apply.

entries.name: Expertly Equipped
entries: Certain features, such as Active Camouflage or a Boarding Harpoon, let your ship double its {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} with a given skill or modification, granting your ship the status of expertly equipped in that skill or modification. As usual, you can only gain expertly equipped status in a skill or modification once.

rows: push your ship to or beyond its limits
slam into an object to deal damage.
Sensor Dampener; {@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb} Device; {@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb} Device, Active Camouflage
allows the ship to remain undetected
pushed a ship beyond its natural limits
access data banks or process data
notice and locate the presence of objects
a general measurement of your ship's beauty and soundness
threaten via ship's appearance or abilities
pass your ship off as something it's not

entries.name: Ability Checks
entries: An {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} represents a ship's ability to overcome a challenge. The GM calls for an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} when a ship, or a crewmember, attempts an action (other than an attack) that has a chance of failure. When the outcome is uncertain, the dice determine the results.

For every {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, the GM decides which of the 6 abilities is relevant to the task at hand and the difficulty of the task, represented by Difficulty Class. The more difficult a task, the higher its DC. The Typical Difficulty Classes table shows the most common DCs.

To make an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, roll a {@dice d20} and add the relevant ability modifier. As with other {@dice d20} rolls, apply bonuses and penalties, and compare the total to the DC. If the total equals or exceeds the DC, the {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} is a success-the ship, or crewmember, overcomes the challenge at hand. Otherwise, it's a failure, which means the ship or crewmember makes no progress toward the objective or makes progress combined with a setback determined by the GM.
When making an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} that involves your ship's abilities, you use the ship's score instead of your own, as dictated by logic.

entries.name: Contests
entries: Sometimes one ship's or crewmember's efforts are directly opposed to another's. This can occur when both of them are trying to do the same thing and only one can succeed, such as attempting to pass through a narrow gap simultaneously. This situation also applies when one of them is trying to prevent the other one from accomplishing a goal—for example, when a ship's gravity projector tries to prevent another ship from jumping to hyperspace. In situations like these, the outcome is determined by a special form of {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, called a contest.

Both participants in a contest make {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} appropriate to their efforts. They apply all appropriate bonuses and penalties, but instead of comparing the total to a DC, they compare the totals of their two checks. The participant with the higher check total wins the contest. That ship or crewmember either succeeds at the action or prevents the other one from succeeding.

If the contest results in a tie, the situation remains the same as it was before the contest. Thus, one contestant might win the contest by default. If two ships tie in a contest to pass through a narrow gap, neither ship makes it. In a contest between a ship's gravity generator trying to prevent another ship from jumping to hyperspace, a tie means that the second ship fails to jump.

entries.name: Passive Checks
entries: A passive check is a special kind of {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} that doesn't involve any die rolls. Such a check can represent the average result for a task done repeatedly, such as probing meteors over and over, or can be used when the GM wants to secretly determine whether the characters succeed at something without rolling dice, such as noticing a hidden ship.

Here's how to determine a ship's total for a passive check: 10 + all modifiers that normally apply to the check. If the ship has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the check, add 5. For {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}, subtract 5. The game refers to a passive check total as a score.
For example. if a 1st-tier ship has a Wisdom of 15 and is proficiently equipped in Scan, it has a passive Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) score of 13.

entries.name: Using Each Ability
entries: Every task that a ship or character might attempt in the game is covered by one of the six abilities. This section explains in more detail what those abilities mean and the ways they are used in the game.

entries.name: Strength
entries: Strength measures the power of a ship's reactor.

entries.name: Strength Checks
entries: Your GM may call for Strength checks when you undergo interactions not covered by skills, such as trying to push through a malleable obstruction like a Conner net.
{@b {@i Ram.}} Use the Ram skill when you want to slam into another object to deal damage.

{@b {@i Boost.}} Use the Boost skill when you attempt to push your ship to or beyond its limits.  A successful Boost check can break ties in straight-line {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} contests or to determine how fast your ship can accelerate to top {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}.  You also make boost checks in response to taking the boost engines, boost shields, and boost weapons actions.

entries.name: Strength Saving Throws
entries: Certain features, such as a Tractor Beam, call for a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. When you make a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you roll a {@dice d20} and add your ship's Strength modifier to the roll. If your ship is proficiently equipped for the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you also add the {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} of the crewmember at the helm to the result of the roll.

entries.name: Damage Rolls
entries: You add your ship's Strength modifier to ship weapon damage rolls.

entries.name: Weapon Hardpoints
entries: While a ship can have any number of hardpoints, it can only Fire a number of times each round equal to the ship's Strength modifier (minimum of +1) times its ship hardpoint size modifier (round up), as shown in the Ship Hardpoint Size modifier table below.  Normally each weapon can only be Fired once per round.

entries.name: Dexterity
entries: Dexterity measures the nimbleness of a ship, as determined by its thrusters and pilot.

entries.name: Dexterity Checks
entries: Your GM may call for Dexterity checks when you undertake actions not covered by skills.

{@b {@i Hide.}} The Hide skill allows the ship to remain undetected by sensors from other ships and stations.  Use the Hide skill when you want to approach a ship or station along a known blind spot, or slink through a debris field, or hide amongst asteroids.

The Hide skill is generally contested by a passive Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) score if the ship's presence is unknown, a Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) check if the presence is suspected or known but the general location is unknown, and an Intelligence ({@skill Probe|sw5e-sotg}) check if the approximate location of a ship is known or suspected.
{@b {@i Maneuvering.}} Use the Maneuvering skill to perform tricky maneuvers in combat, to deftly fly through an asteroid field, and to impress others with flying skills.
When you would make a Dexterity ({@skill Maneuvering|sw5e-sotg}) check, you may instead make an Intelligence ({@skill Piloting|sw5e-phb}) check at {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.
Your ship is considered proficiently equipped in this skill if the crewmember at the helm is proficient in {@skill Piloting|sw5e-phb}.
Your ship is considered expertly equipped in this skill if the crewmember at the helm has {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in {@skill Piloting|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Hiding
entries: When you try to hide your ship, make a Dexterity ({@skill Hide|sw5e-sotg}) check. Until you are discovered or stop hiding, that check is contested by the Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) check of any ship or station that actively searches for signs of your presence. You can't hide from a ship that can perceive you, and if your ship does something to make your ship noticed, you give away your position. In combat, most ships stay alert for danger, so if you come out of hiding and approach a ship, it usually per-ceives you. However, under certain circumstances, the GM might allow you to stay hidden as you approach a ship that is distracted or has some blind spot or de-fect, allowing you to gain {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on an attack before you are perceived. {@b {@i Passive Scan.}} When you hide, there's a chance some-one will notice you even if they aren't searching. To determine whether such a ship notices you, the GM compares your Dexterity ({@skill Hide|sw5e-sotg}) check with that ship's passive Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) score, which equals 10 + the ship's Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) modifier. If the ship has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}, add 5. For {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}, subtract 5. For example, if a 1st-tier ship has a Wisdom of 15 and is proficiently equipped for Scan, it has a passive Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) of 14.

entries.name: Dexterity Saving Throws
entries: Certain features, such as burst weapons, call for a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. When you make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you roll a {@dice d20} and add your ship's Dexterity modifier to the roll. If your ship is proficiently equipped for the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you also add the {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} of the crewmember at the helm to the result of the roll.

entries.name: Alternative INITIATIVE
entries: At the beginning of every combat, instead of rolling {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative}, GMs can quickly use passive initiatives to determine order based on a ship's Dexterity and it's ship size base {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} as shown below in the Starship Size Base {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb} table below. ##### Starship Size Base {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb}
To calculate a ship's passive {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative}, use the following formula: {@b initiative = "ship size base initiative" + "Dexterity modifier"}

entries.name: Constitution
entries: Constitution represents the durability of a ship's hull.

entries.name: Constitution Checks
entries: Your GM may call for a Constitution check when you undergo interactions not covered by skills, such as overcoming the debilitating nature of an ion storm.

{@b {@i Patch.}} You can attempt to have the ship patch up damage it has taken, using one of its Hull Dice. When you take the {@variantrule Patch|sw5e-sotg} action, you make a Constitution ({@skill Patch|sw5e-sotg}) check (DC = 10 or half the ship's missing hull points, whichever number is higher). On a failure, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the Hull Dice roll. On a success you roll the Hull Die normally.

When you would make a Constitution ({@skill Patch|sw5e-sotg}) check, you may instead make an Intelligence ({@item Mechanic's kit|sw5e-phb|Mechanic's Kit}) check at {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} using your own Intelligence modifier.
{@b {@i Regulation.}} Your GM may require a Regulation check when your ship is pushed beyond its natural limits.  Situations which might call for a Regulation check include:

items: Trying to reach safety on low fuel
In response to a mechanic straining the reactor
Attempting to run at top {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} for long periods of time
Keeping life support running when out of fuel.

entries: When you would make a Constitution ({@skill Regulation|sw5e-sotg}) check, you may instead make an Intelligence ({@item Mechanic's kit|sw5e-phb|Mechanic's Kit}) check at {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} using your own Intelligence modifier.

entries.name: Constitution Saving Throws
entries: Certain features, such as a {@item Heavy ion cannon|sw5e-sotg}, call for a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. When you make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you roll a {@dice d20} and add your ship's Constitution modifier to the roll. If your ship is proficiently equipped in the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you also add the {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} of the crewmember at the helm to the result of the roll.

entries.name: Hull Points
entries: Your ship's Constitution modifier contributes to its hull points. Typically, your ship adds its Constitution modifier to each Hull Die it rolls for its hull points.

If your ship's Constitution modifier changes, its hull point maximum changes as well, as though it had the new modifier from tier 0. For instance, if your Small ship's Constitution modifier increases from +1 to +2 when it reaches 1st tier, you adjust its hull point maximum as though the modifier had always been +2. So you add 3 hull points for tier 0, and then roll your hull points for tier 1 using your new modifier. Additionally, if some effect lowers your ship's Constitution score so as to reduce its Constitution modifier by 1, its hull point maximum is reduced as well.

entries.name: Suites
entries: A ship's maximum number of suites is based on its size and Constitution modifier.

entries.name: Intelligence
entries: Intelligence represents the capability of the ship's computers, determines its minimum crew size, and affects its discrimination, calculation, and memory functions.

entries.name: Intelligence Checks
entries: An Intelligence check comes into play when you need to draw on the ship's ability to process large amounts of data and sensory input, to access esoteric data, calculate complex mathematical problems or to deal with computer slicing. The Astrogation, Data, and Probe skills reflect aptitude in certain kinds of Intelligence checks.
{@b {@i Astrogation.}} Make an Astrogation check to calculate hyperspace jumps.  For more details on making Astrogation checks, see the "Travel in Hyperspace" section of Chapter 8.

When you would make an Intelligence ({@skill Astrogation|sw5e-sotg}) check, you may instead make an Intelligence ({@skill Technology|sw5e-phb}) check at {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} using your own Intelligence modifier.

{@b {@i Data.}} Use the Data skill when you want to access your ship's data banks to learn information about appropriate information.  Ships often have standard information about hyperlanes, systems, planets, and other astronomical information.  Ships can also be upgraded to include more detailed information or information on other subjects.  The more obscure the information or the more off-topic, the higher the DC should be.

{@b {@i Probe.}} When you focus your ship's sensor suite on an area or ship and investigate in detail, you make an Intelligence ({@skill Probe|sw5e-sotg}) check.  A successful check may reveal the location of a hidden ship, may indicate the presence of physical damage in a construct or of minerals in an asteroid, or may provide technical details about a ship you have probed or the presence of lifeforms on board.

When you would make an Intelligence ({@skill Probe|sw5e-sotg}) check, you may instead make an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}) check at {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} using your own Intelligence modifier.

entries.name: Intelligence Saving Throws
entries: Certain features call for an Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. When you make an Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you roll a {@dice d20} and add your ship's Intelligence modifier to the roll. If your ship is proficiently equipped in the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you also add the {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} of the crewmember at the helm to the result of the roll.

entries.name: Wisdom
entries: Wisdom represents the capability of the ship's targeting, sensors, and awareness of its surroundings.

entries.name: Wisdom Checks
entries: A Wisdom check comes into play when you need to draw on the ship's ability to sense its surroundings, perceive threats, and filter electromagnetic fields. The Scan skill reflects aptitude in certain kinds of Wisdom checks.

{@b {@i Scan.}} Your Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) check lets you notice and locate the presence of something near your ship. It measures your general awareness of the ship's surroundings and the keenness of your ship's detection algorithms.

When you would make a Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) check, you may instead make a Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) check at {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} using your own Wisdom modifier.

entries.name: Wisdom Saving Throws
entries: Certain features call for a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. When you make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you roll a {@dice d20} and add your ship's Wisdom modifier to the roll. If your ship is proficiently equipped in the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you also add the {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} of the crewmember at the helm to the result of the roll.

entries.name: Attack Rolls and Weapon Saves
entries: You add your ship's Wisdom modifier to ship {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack rolls} and to the DC of saves called for by ship weapons.

entries.name: Charisma
entries: Charisma represents the presence of the ship, including its prestige and the clarity, sophistication, and power of the ship's communications and interference equipment.

entries.name: Charisma Checks
entries: A Charisma check comes into play when you need to command and influence others characters and ships with your own ship. The Impress, Interfere, Menace, and Swindle skills reflect aptitude in certain kinds of Charisma checks.

{@b {@i Impress.}} The Impress skill is a general measurement of your ship's beauty and soundness.  Whether or not your ship {@i is} impressively outfitted and well maintained, does it {@i look} impressively outfitted and well maintained?  Does your on-board cantina {@i look} opulent?

When you would make a Charisma ({@skill Impress|sw5e-sotg}) check, you may instead choose to make a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}) check at {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} using your own Charisma modifier.

{@b {@i Interfere.}} When you attempt to interfere with another ship or creature you use the Interfere skill.  When you would make a Charisma ({@skill Interfere|sw5e-sotg}) check, you may instead choose to make an Intelligence ({@item Slicer's kit|sw5e-phb|Slicer's Kit}) check at {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} using your own Intelligence modifier.

{@b {@i Menace.}} When you attempt to influence someone through the threat of your ship's abilities, whether {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, firepower, or toughness, the GM might ask you to make a Charisma ({@skill Menace|sw5e-sotg}) check.  Alternatively, you may make a Charisma (Intimidate) check at {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} using your own Charisma modifier.
{@b {@i Swindle.}} Use the Swindle skill when you want to pass your ship off as something it's not.  Examples of using the Swindle skill include:

items: passing off a heavily armed ship as a simple freighter
concealing the presence of lifeforms on your ship
concealing the presence of hidden cargo.

entries: When you would make a Charisma ({@skill Swindle|sw5e-sotg}) check, you may instead choose to make a Charisma ({@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}) check at {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} using your own Charisma modifier.

entries.name: Charisma Saving Throws
entries: Certain features call for a Charisma {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. When you make a Charisma {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you roll a {@dice d20} and add your ship's Charisma modifier to the roll. If your ship is proficiently equipped in the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you also add the {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} of the crewmember at the helm to the result of the roll.

data.name: Chapter 8: Adventuring
entries: Diving through an asteroid field, docking in a space port, or simply exploring the wild blue yonder, are the things that {@i Star Wars} adventures are made of. Your character, with the aid of their ship, might explore wild space, undertake dangerous smuggling missions, or dispatch pirate ships. And if all goes well, your character will survive to claim rich rewards before embarking on a new adventure.

This chapter covers the basics of adventuring in space, from the mechanics of movement to the acquisition of the ship itself. The rules for repair are also in this chapter, along with a discussion of the activities your characters might pursue between adventures.
Whether adventurers are exploring uncharted territories or a complicated relationship with a criminal organization, the game follows a natural rhythm, as outlined in the book's introduction:
{@b 1. The GM describes the environment.} {@b 2. The players describe what they want to do.} {@b 3. The GM narrates the results of their actions.}
Typically, the GM uses a map as an outline of the adventure, tracking the characters' progress as they explore enclave corridors or wilderness regions.

The GM's notes, including a key to the map, describe what the adventurers find as they enter each new area. Sometimes, the passage of time and the adventurers' actions determine what happens, so the GM might use a timeline or a flowchart to track their progress instead of a map.

entries.name: Ship Registration
entries: Pilots are required to register their starships with the Bureau of Ships and Services (or BoSS). Additionally, at registration, the pilot must acquire an Operating License at the cost of 1,000 credits. To be eligible for this license they must pass a written piloting test, which requires a DC 15 Intelligence ({@skill Piloting|sw5e-phb}) check.

entries.name: Transponder Codes
entries: When ships are created, they are assigned a unique signal called a transponder code. Once registered with the BoSS, this signal can be used to identify that ship using the BoSS database. The transponder code can be used to identify a ship's owner, designation, make and model, as well as any registered modifications. Additionally, a transponder code can be used to access the ship's ownership history.
The transponder code is built into the ship's sublight engines, making any attempt to remove or alter it incredibly difficult; failing an attempt could damage or destroy a ship's engines.

entries.name: The Bureau of Ships and Services
entries: The Bureau of Ships and Services (BoSS) is a long-standing, impartial, third-party galactic organization that manages all data related to the massive number of starships present in the galaxy. The BoSS has stood for thousands of years due to their ability to stay neutral in conflicts. Information on a ship's ownership and its captains certifications are kept on file at the BoSS at all times. The data is distributed to spaceports upon request, but it is an expensive and slow process. As a result of this, smaller spaceports rarely update their registries more than once a year. The security on BoSS computer systems is of the highest caliber money can buy, making it almost impossible to access without proper authorization codes.

entries.name: Communications
entries: Starships are equipped with basic systems that allow for communication in realspace. Typically, starship communications systems are limited to contact ships and planets within the same system, although boosters and specialized radios can reach up to several light-years. Opening a channel to a willing recipient is simply a matter of pinging their ship. They will receive a notification and can respond, opening the lines of communication.

entries.name: HoloNet
entries: The Holonet is an instantaneous communication system that allows planets to stay in contact despite the vast distances between them. A HoloNet transceiver transmits and receives information through hyperspace, allowing information to travel millions of times faster than the {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} of light. Hyperwave transceivers are embedded at strategic locations, constantly relaying information throughout the galaxy. This networks allows for instantaneous three-dimensional holographic communications at virtually any distance, making it one of the primary means of communication. Government agencies, such as the military, typically maintain their own encrypted circuits on the HoloNet. Some experienced slicers have been able to access these encrypted channels, though it required access to a government compound for the requisite codes.

entries.name: METOSP (Message to Spacers)
entries: Upon arrival in a star system, most starships immediately connect to a specialized frequency responsible for communicating with incoming and outbound ships, called Message to Spacers, or METOSP. The METOSP message typically conveys a repeated greeting with information about flight hazards (such as blockades, weather, debris, or collisions) and relevant local regulations or customs (such as embargoes, tariffs, or landing procedures). All METOSPs are broadcast in {@language Galactic Basic|sw5e-phb}, though some worlds also broadcast in their native language. A METOSP provides pilots with contact information for spaceport control as well as information on landing patterns and traffic lanes. Most METOSPs are brief, repeating messages that refer listeners to other channels for specific information.

entries.name: Planetary Information Channels
entries: Most planets also provide incoming space traffic with basic computer communication channels. These channels connect the ship to planetary information networks that provide everything from communications directory assistance to tourism information and planetary maps. Planetary information channels allow use of the {@skill Technology|sw5e-phb} skill to access information relevant to the planet, and it possible for a slicer to access other functions.

entries.name: Time
entries: In situations where keeping track of the passage of time is important, the GM determines the time a task requires. The GM might use a different time scale depending on the context of the situation at hand. In an enclosed environment, the adventurers' movement happens on a scale of minutes. It takes them about a minute to navigate an asteroid field, a minute to dock in a space port, and a good 10 minutes to clear customs.
While traveling in realspace, a scale of hours is often more appropriate. Adventurers eager to reach a pirate stronghold on the other side of the planet travel those 150 miles in just over an hour.
In hyerspace, however, a scale of days works best. Following the hyperlane from Tatooine to Kashyyyk, the adventurers spend four uneventful days before a pirate ambush interrupts their journey.
In combat and other fast-paced situations, the game relies on rounds, a 6-second span of time described in chapter 9.

entries.name: Movement and Travel
entries: There are two significant travel types: Realspace and Hyperspace.

entries.name: Travel in Realspace
entries: All starships have sublight engines that propel them through realspace, using them when taking off, landing, or flying within a gravity sphere.

When traveling in realspace, the GM can summarize the adventurers' movement without calculating exact distances or travel times: "You fly around the planet, reaching the stronghold late in the evening."

Sometimes it's important, though, to know how far, how fast, and how maneuverable your ship is in a short window of time. Starships come equipped with two speeds: {@b flying speed} and {@b turning speed}.

entries.name: Flying Speed
entries: {@b Flying speed} is how far your ship can travel in a single round. It is expressed in feet. For every foot your ship travels forward, it expends one foot from its {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}.
A ship's unmodified flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is determined in {@book Chapter 3: Starships|sw5e-sotg|5|Chapter 3: Starships} by the Role selected for the ship at construction.

entries.name: Turning Speed
entries: {@b Turning speed} determines how maneuverable your ship is. In order for your ship to rotate 90 degrees, you must spend an amount of your {@b flying speed} equal to your {@b turning speed}. For instance, if your ship has a {@b flying speed} of 350 feet, and a {@b turning speed} of 100 feet, you can travel 150 feet in a straight line, spending 150 feet of your {@b flying speed}, and then turn 90 degrees to starboard, spending 100 feet of your {@b flying speed}, leaving 100 feet of movement remaining.
Typically games are played with turning limited to 90 degree increments, but, if your group has the desire and capability to track smaller angles, this is allowed.
A ship can turn more (or less, if your group agrees) than 90 degrees on its turn, by spending a proportionate amount of movement.

If a ship's turning {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} exceeds its flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, that ship cannot turn 90 degrees, in combat conditions, absent another effect modifiying the ship's turning {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} and/or flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} or the Hard Turn action.
A ship's unmodified turning {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is determined in {@book Chapter 3: Starships|sw5e-sotg|5|Chapter 3: Starships} by the Role selected for the ship at construction.

entries.name: Travel Pace
entries: While traveling in realspace, a starship can move at a normal, fast, or slow pace. While traveling at a fast pace, your starship's flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is doubled, but your starship—and its crew—have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Intelligence ({@skill Probe|sw5e-sotg}) and Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) checks. While traveling at a slow pace, your flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is halved, but you can travel stealthily. A fast pace makes a ship less perceptive, while a slow pace makes it possible to sneak around and to search an area more carefully (see the "Activity While Traveling" section later in this chapter for more information).
You can use the following {@b Sample Realspace Travel Times} table to determine travel times in realspace for an average starship traveling at a normal pace.

rows: Orbit to safe hyperspace jump distance
Orbit to another planet in the same system
Orbit to outer edge of system

entries.name: Difficult Terrain
